Top Wall Street analysts prefer these 3 dividend stocks for stable income

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade.
  • Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a manufacturer's ability to pay dividends consistently.
  • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a manufacturer's ability to pay dividends consistently.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The company has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.

It has been revealed that in an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the manufacturer's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

Industry observers note that specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

Furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in new wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

It has been revealed that "While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," said Mehta.

Industry observers note that mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.

In a recent development, kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream company operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.

According to recent reports, ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst John Mackay reiterated a buy rating on Kinetik stock and slightly raised his price target to $58 from $57. He expects the company to report Q3 2026 EBITDA of $279 million, higher than the Street's expectation of $270 million but lower than the second quarter's EBITDA of $281 million.

The 5-star analyst expects Kinetik's Q3 performance to gain from higher gas volumes after notable curtailments in the second quarter. Mackay also expects the quarter to benefit from higher production and steady commodity margins, even though some lower-margin contracts and weaker Waha spread marketing gains could weigh on results.

Overall, Mackay increased his Q3 2026 estimates to reflect higher volumes, driven by rapid Permian egress pipeline commissioning, stronger throughput at Kings Landing I, and higher M2M commodity prices, offset by increased costs.

"As natural gas takeaway constraints ease across the Permian, investor focus centers on KNTK's YE26 volume trajectory and durability of its multi-year growth," said Mackay.

Mackay ranks No. 569 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.9%. See Kinetik's Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Moving to Crescent Energy (CRGY), an exploration and production company with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian, and Uinta Basins. With a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share (annualized dividend of $0.48 per share), CRGY's dividend yield stands at 3.56%. Earlier this month, Crescent declared an agreement to acquire Eagle Ford assets from Devon Energy (DVN).

Heading into Q3 earnings on Nov. 2, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reiterated a buy rating on Crescent stock and slightly lowered the price target to $17 from $18, citing dilution from upcoming shares.

"CRGY's recent acquisition of DVN's Eagle Ford assets marks a strategic, growth-oriented move, potentially enhancing cash flow performance," remarked Richardson.

The 5-star analyst noted that the acquisition of the Eagle Ford assets at a net purchase price of $3.85 billion will add about 68 MBoe/d of net production and over 600 net Tier 1 locations. Richardson added that a solid track record of synergies from past deals in the Eagle Ford region increases confidence about Crescent achieving efficiencies with this deal.

Additionally, Richardson noted that the financial implications of the acquisition seem impressive, with a projected increase in cash flow per share of about 9% for 2027 to 2029.

The analyst believes that Crescent is not just expanding its business through acquisitions but positioning itself as a more durable tech giant, regardless of market conditions.

Richardson ranks No. 478 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Crescent Energy Statistics on TipRanks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points lower than yesterday and three basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

According to recent reports, A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today. While the economy never sleeps, markets are closed on the weekends. The rates you see Friday are unlikely to change much (if at all) until Monday.

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Recent findings suggest that next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a substantial reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

If PCE indicates inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

Recent findings suggest that I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index indicated wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.74% or higher.

In a recent development, also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

Recent findings suggest that » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a upcoming home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

In a recent development, » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Arizona Cardinals fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis on Monday, a day after a 34-7 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.

Industry observers note that head coach Mike LaFleur confirmed Rallis' dismissal in his weekly news conference. He said the decision to fire Rallis was made out of a need for a "fresh perspective.".

"Nick's a guy that I have a lot of respect for as a person, as a coach," LaFleur said. "… I just felt in my heart this morning that we needed a change. We needed a fresh perspective, a fresh voice.".

Senior defensive assistant Teryl Austin will take over as interim defensive coordinator. Austin has previously worked as the defensive coordinator for the Lions, Bengals and Steelers, most recently with Pittsburgh from 2022-25.

Sunday's loss dropped the Cardinals to 3-8. They've allowed 30-plus points in eight of their 11 games and rank 31st in the NFL with 29.4 points allowed per game. They rank 26th with 355.2 yards allowed per game.

The Cardinals have plenty of challenges beyond their defense. They rank 25th in total offense (290 ypg) and 29th in scoring (17.4 ppg) as the owners of the worst record in the NFC.

In a recent development, former Broncos head coach Nathaniel Hackett is Arizona's offensive coordinator. Hackett has had four previous stops as an NFL offensive coordinator, including for LaFleur's brother, Matt LaFleur, with the Green Bay Packers. Mike LaFleur acknowledged Monday that the Cardinals need to improve across the board.

In a recent development, "It's not been good enough collectively, all phases as a team. I'm in the business, and it's my job to find solutions, and this is one that we're trying to find. ….

Recent findings suggest that "We're all in this thing together. If you're a real man in this league, you're gonna look at yourself in the mirror first.".

College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1384 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
  • Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's crucial to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
  • Scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's crucial to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

Scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

In a recent development, these scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

Some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s vital to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

According to recent reports, merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

It has been revealed that merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

Sources indicate that merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

Recent findings suggest that some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that highlights more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

Unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

Recent findings suggest that some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

Athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

Even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

Sources indicate that some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

According to recent reports, scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

Which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

It has been revealed that veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

It has been revealed that scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

According to recent reports, the best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

Think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

Sources indicate that apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a significant impact when you add several of them together.

Understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

Sources indicate that not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

    Tech Report: Dreading Holiday Money Talks With Family? Here's What to Say

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (798 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Holiday gatherings have a way of stirring up difficult and downright uncomfortable conversations — and not just about politics or cousin Derek’s love life.
    • Relatives and friends may also bring up their money troubles and financial plans.
    • It has been revealed that it’s easy to feel obligated or pressured to help out.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Holiday gatherings have a way of stirring up difficult and downright uncomfortable conversations — and not just about politics or cousin Derek’s love life.

    Relatives and friends may also bring up their money troubles and financial plans. That might involve asking you to lend money or your credit.

    It has been revealed that it’s easy to feel obligated or pressured to help out. But it’s key to establish boundaries so you don’t end up making a decision you’ll regret.

    If you suspect a money request is coming your way, think carefully about what you’re willing — and able — to offer. You might choose a specific dollar limit or to give no financial help at all.

    “Only lend what you're truly OK losing,” says Alvin Carlos, a certified financial planner at District Capital Management in Washington, D.C. “Look at your budget and decide what you could hand over and never see again.”.

    Choose the language that best fits your situation. Adapt your responses as needed to guide the conversation in a direction that works for you.

    “I understand that you need help. I just need to review my own finances before I can give you an answer. I’ll get back to you by [day].”.

    If the request comes up at a holiday or family gathering:.

    Industry observers note that “I’d rather discuss this privately. Let’s find another time to talk.”.

    “Here's what I’m comfortable with, and here's what I have to protect to be financially safe, mentally safe, and to continue to be there for you in the ways that you need me.”Or, if you want to be more direct:.

    Sometimes, there’s an unspoken expectation to give money because of how much loved ones think you earn, notes Ashley Agnew, a certified financial therapist in Boston.

    Getting ahead of it before there's a tipping point can help with tricky dynamics, she notes.

    A recent Edward Jones report found that only about one-third of financial caregiving arrangements were planned and discussed in advance. The report also found that nearly half of financial caregivers (49%) make financial sacrifices, such as reducing or stopping saving, or tapping into their retirement account.

    Factor your financial health, your values and emotional well-being into your decision:.

    Review your income, expenses and savings. If you provide financial help and don’t get the money back, would you struggle to pay bills or reach financial goals? Prioritize building an emergency fund, saving for retirement and paying off high-interest debt first, Carlos says.

    Consider your relationship. Would you feel resentful if you aren’t repaid? How do you think your friend or relative would react if you decline to help? Could it damage your relationship, and if so, is it worth it?

    Industry observers note that understand the credit risks. Co-signing or allowing someone else to use your credit can leave you responsible for payments and expose you to potential credit damage.

    Know the tax implications. If you’re considering a substantial gift or loan, check with a tax professional about any reporting requirements and tax consequences.

    Recent findings suggest that consult your partner. If you share finances, make sure to include your partner in your decision-making process, Agnew says. If you have a parent asking for financial assistance, for example, but your cultural view is different from your spouse's, that’s a big opportunity for a rift.

    Aim to be clear and direct. When in doubt, keep your answer concise, Agnew says.

    “Keeping it short and sweet will communicate that you've made a decision, not that you've requested a negotiation.”.

    Depending on where you left the conversation, you might have more steps to take.

    Stick to your boundaries and promises. Did you offer to contribute money? Pay as agreed. Did you say no? Don’t let your friend's or family member’s persistence, or the opinions of other friends and relatives, change your mind.

    If you offered to provide nonfinancial support, Carlos recommends pointing your loved one to local government and nonprofit resources. That might include emergency rent assistance, cheap or free financial advice, food banks and career services.

    Sources indicate that document the details and set the plan in motion. If you agreed to loan money, send your relative a quick text recapping the terms, Carlos says. He also suggests setting up a simple repayment system together, such as a recurring Zelle or Venmo transfer.

    “Fewer reminders from you mean less tension,” he says.

    Get outside help, if necessary. Despite your best efforts, it can be difficult to handle the situation on your own. If you’re feeling lingering stress or your family can’t reach a resolution, you might want to bring in some help, Agnew claims.

    She recommends working with a financial therapist or advisor, or using a financial wellness app.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    • In a recent development, robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    It has been revealed that here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    In a recent development, robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    Sources indicate that robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly notable sources of transaction revenue, while the tech giant has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    According to recent reports, transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Recent findings suggest that net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mortgage rates have had some substantial day-over-day swings lately, and today, unfortunately it's an upward swing.
    • The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.
    • Recent findings suggest that recently news about significant tech has often pulled rates down.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates have had some substantial day-over-day swings lately, and today, unfortunately it's an upward swing.

    The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points higher than yesterday and four basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    Recent findings suggest that recently news about significant tech has often pulled rates down. Investor concerns about AI profitability keep cropping up, and when they do, tech stocks and bonds lose their appeal and Treasuries have been picking up the slack. Mortgage rates are generally benchmarked to the yield on the 10-year Treasury, and Treasury prices and yields move inversely. More demand for the 10YT drives prices up, and sends yields (and thus, mortgage rates) down.

    It has been revealed that today's the opposite, though. Investors are having a bout of tech exuberance as Jensen Huang got reinstated as Nvidia CEO, and lots of excitement about tech stocks and bonds means less enthusiasm for Treasuries.

    Here's the thing, though: Markets are fickle. They also move fast. And they aren't the only influence on mortgage rates.

    Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    Sources indicate that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to latest inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Industry observers note that lately, we've seen two narratives influencing mortgage rates battling it out; depending on which one's stronger, daily rates move higher or lower. Up top I talked about how shifting perceptions of significant tech have been driving mortgage rates (and yes, today, pushing them higher, though usually it's pulled rates down.) When rates are moving higher, more often it's been thanks to inflation — and while it's a lightweight work week, we're about to get heavyweight inflation news.

    The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely.

    The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation, so you can guess how things are likely to go at the Fed's December meeting. Markets already feel fairly certain about a quarter-percent rate hike.

    According to recent reports, we already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three significant inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI demonstrated wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

    Industry observers note that predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out Wednesday morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    And speaking of: Markets will be closed on Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, so we'll all have a bit of a break this week. Mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

    P.S.: I don't have to ask if anyone's playing Grand Theft Auto 'cause c'mon, of course. But did anyone else perk up when Lu asked about home loans? Yeah, that was probably just me. Jason and Lucia would have to change a lot about their lifestyle to qualify (we know they're working on building credit, but having all your income be cash you can't really document is not going to work for a lender). But hey, I'm rooting for them.

    » Learn more: How the Fed affects mortgage rates.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you blueprint to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.88% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

    Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    Industry observers note that » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    It has been revealed that if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    Prediction: This Will Be Sandisk’s Stock Price by the End of 2027

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (788 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sandisk (SNDK +10.69%) has been one of the more notable tech growth stories over the last two years.
    • It has been revealed that unfortunately, the stock began a dramatic downturn from that peak over the summer, and it’s now down by more than 70% from its high.
    • When comparing the firm's continued growth and the expectations surrounding its industry, I believe Sandisk stock could end 2027 in the $170-per-share range.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Will Healy – Nov 23, 2026 at 4:56PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Sandisk ›.

    Sandisk (SNDK +10.69%) has been one of the more notable tech growth stories over the last two years. After Western Digital spun it back off in February of last year, the stock rose by as much as 6,400%.

    It has been revealed that unfortunately, the stock began a dramatic downturn from that peak over the summer, and it’s now down by more than 70% from its high. That did not stop Sandisk management from initiating an 8-for-1 stock split that took place Friday. Nonetheless, that volatility calls the stock's state into question, particularly when you’re trying to predict where it will trade at the end of 2027.

    When comparing the firm's continued growth and the expectations surrounding its industry, I believe Sandisk stock could end 2027 in the $170-per-share range.

    Sandisk operates in one of the most volatile parts of the tech industry: memory. It specializes in NAND, a non-volatile type of memory that is used for longer-term storage, as well as in solid-state drives.

    In a recent development, western Digital bought the manufacturer back in 2016, but since it spun it back off again as a separate company, Sandisk has prospered. The rapid surge in AI data center construction has led to a severe shortage of the types of memory it supplies, giving Sandisk unusually strong pricing power. The result has been soaring revenues, wide profit margins, and a much higher stock price.

    Sources indicate that unfortunately for investors, memory-chip makers are among the most volatile players in the chip industry. Memory products are fairly commoditized — there’s not a lot of differentiation between the NAND made by Sandisk and that sold by its direct peers. For this reason, prices are tightly linked to the supply-and-demand dynamic. Eventually, supply will catch up to demand and Sandisk will lose much of its pricing power.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Recent findings suggest that additionally, despite rapid growth, headwinds in the AI industry are emerging as investors question whether it can maintain current levels of capital expenditures (capex) amid rising interest rates. If capital becomes more scarce, the pace of the AI build-out could slow.

    All of those conditions make it difficult to tell whether Sandisk is a bargain or a value trap.

    Sources indicate that right now, Sandisk trades at around 5 times earnings. However, memory stock investors know the both revenue and profits can reverse dramatically during an industry downturn. History suggests that investors should not perceive that valuation as a "bargain.".

    Despite those risks, Sandisk's immediate future appears too compelling to dismiss.

    In its fiscal 2027, which will end in July 2027, analysts forecast it will bring in just under $50 billion in revenue. If that prediction proves accurate, it will amount to a 145% year-over-year increase. Analysts also expect net earnings of $28.44 per share. On a split-adjusted basis, it earned $8.86 per share in its fiscal 2026.

    Looking forward into fiscal 2028, analysts forecast revenue growth will slow to 24%. That could generate negative sentiment, but the $36.13 in consensus earnings expected that year would leave the P/E ratio at 2.4 at the current share price of $79 per share. That appears unreasonably low.

    Nonetheless, whatever the sentiment, $28.44 per share multiplied by 6 — a common earnings multiple for memory stocks — would leave Sandisk with an approximate price of $170 per share. That factor alone makes it difficult to believe that Sandisk will not rise again.

    Considering the forces that will likely pull Sandisk in opposing directions, I believe the stock will end 2027 in the neighborhood of $170, and trading at a P/E of about 6.

    Sources indicate that admittedly, with the stock seemingly in free fall now, this might be a controversial call. The pricing power that Sandisk commands for now could disappear if the AI bubble bursts.

    According to recent reports, however, for now, an AI bust is more fear than reality. Additionally, we know that Sandisk’s bottom line will be far higher by the end of 2027. Unless the industry completely falls apart, it is hard to imagine that Sandisk stock will not trade at a much higher price by the end of next year.

    #97089. Breaking: I Rate Buy Now, Pay Later Apps; Here’s My Holiday Advice

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (980 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: I Rate Buy Now, Pay Later Apps; Here’s My Holiday Advice

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (980 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As Americans compile their shopping lists ahead of the holiday season, I’ve been compiling my own kind of list — a list of 25 data points, gathered across six “buy now, pay later” (BNPL) apps, fed into a rubric of five categories and 22 subcategories, to produce a star rating for each app.
    • Sources indicate that it’s a significant list.
    • By the end, I know more about these apps than anyone should, and I’m eager to bestow my knowledge on the next unsuspecting person who utters “Klarna” in my vicinity.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As Americans compile their shopping lists ahead of the holiday season, I’ve been compiling my own kind of list — a list of 25 data points, gathered across six “buy now, pay later” (BNPL) apps, fed into a rubric of five categories and 22 subcategories, to produce a star rating for each app.

    Sources indicate that it’s a significant list. I check it twice (or 10 times).

    By the end, I know more about these apps than anyone should, and I’m eager to bestow my knowledge on the next unsuspecting person who utters “Klarna” in my vicinity.

    I should have plenty of opportunities this year. Nearly 2 in 5 holiday spenders (38%) proposal to use BNPL, according to NerdWallet’s holiday spending report. Concerningly, the same report found that a higher share of BNPL customers expect they won’t be able to make their payments in full and on time compared to credit card users.

    Using BNPL for holiday shopping isn’t inherently bad, but there are risks, including sneaky fees and the ease of loan stacking across many providers.

    Here’s how to minimize those risks and set yourself up for success this holiday season.

    Sources indicate that brenton Harrison, a certified financial planner in Nashville, says many of his clients are turning to buy now, pay later in the “messy middle of life,” when everyday expenses are high and budgets are tight. This is especially true during the holidays.

    “They have kids they're providing for, or they’re trying to go travel and see family,” Harrison says. “When those expenses pile up, it can be very attractive to be able to spread out payments.”.

    Since BNPL divides your total purchase into smaller installments, typically due every two weeks, it feels easier on your cash flow than having to pay all at once.

    While Harrison is open to his clients using BNPL, he emphasizes how important it is to understand the terms before opting in. BNPL apps only require a soft credit pull and a short application. When you can apply for a loan in just a few clicks, it’s easy to miss when payments are due or whether they’ll include interest.

    But if clients understand the terms and are certain they can make the payments, Harrison says BNPL's set repayment schedule can be a better option than more open-ended financing.

    “With a credit card, [a holiday purchase] might be something that they buy over and over and over again, because that interest just continues to accrue over time, and they never pay it off,” he says.

    According to recent reports, not all BNPL apps are created equal. I measure the top apps across multiple categories, but I weigh affordability the highest. My thinking is if you’re already strapped for cash, it’s a bad idea to pay extra just to break up the payments.

    Recent findings suggest that there are providers, like Affirm and PayPal, that don’t charge interest with a common pay-in-four term (your total purchase, divided into four installments). They also charge no fees, including no late fees for missed payments.

    Compare that to apps, like Sezzle and Zip, that may charge an automatic service or origination fee with your first installment, as well as late fees.

    Long-term BNPL financing, which can stretch months or even years, usually includes interest, expressed as an annual percentage rate or APR. This is a more expensive payment option than a zero-interest pay-in-four.

    Sources indicate that pay close attention to your checkout screen to see what you’re offered. Are the installment amounts equal or is the first installment higher than the others? That may mean there’s a fee. Do you see an APR listed? That means you’re paying interest.

    According to recent reports, harrison points out that just because a store partners with a BNPL firm doesn’t mean that’s your only option. Download a different BNPL app, search for the store and see if you get access to better terms, like a 0% offer.

    Taking out multiple loans with different BNPL providers is known as “loan stacking,” and it’s risky.

    Because you’re juggling different payment amounts due on different days, it’s hard to keep track of what’s coming out of your bank account. This is especially true if you set up automatic payments, which most BNPL apps require. If you overdraw your checking account, your bank will likely charge a fee.

    In a recent development, according to research published in August by the Federal Reserve, 11% percent of BNPL users had a BNPL payment trigger an overdraft or nonsufficient funds fee from their bank in the prior year. People with less savings were even more likely to pay fees.

    Before applying for multiple BNPL loans, look at a typical month of expenses and ask if there’s extra room in your budget for those payments, Harrison says.

    According to recent reports, “If you’re just assuming that because you’re spreading it out that you’ll be able to pay it, that's where I think people can get in trouble,” he states. “They set it and forget it, and they don't realize, ‘Oh, I am in no better position to pay that next month than I am this month, or I have three of these going at the same time, and collectively, it's more than I can manage.’”.

    Most apps send payment reminders, so you can potentially reschedule the payment or change your payment method.

    Still, it’s best to avoid the headache to begin with. If you’re feeling pressured to spend more this holiday season, communicate your limits clearly with loved ones, Harrison states, and avoid any loans you can’t comfortably repay.

    “Think about the purchase itself, especially around the holidays,” he says. “There's a massive difference between something that I can pay off over three months and something that I should have never been buying in the first place.”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Week 11 of the NFL season is almost completed with the Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) and Washington Commanders (3-5-1) set to play on Monday night.

    The week began with Thursday night's matchup between the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans. The Texans prevailed 26-3 as the Colts performed so poorly offensively that the team decided to move on from quarterback Daniel Jones and released him the next day.

    Jones' next destination will be one of the NFL's top stories as Week 11 finishes and the season progresses toward Week 12. The eight-year veteran is expected to clear waivers on Monday and from there, he will wait to see what his best option is, according to ESPN. Among the teams that could line up to sign him are the Arizona Cardinals, New England Patriots and Baltimore Ravens.

    According to recent reports, the San Francisco 49ers defeated the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City to close out Sunday's slate. With the 35-10 victory, the Niners improved to 9-1 to keep hold of the top seed in the NFC. The Buffalo Bills matched them for the NFL's best mark with a 26-9 win over the Miami Dolphins.

    Industry observers note that one concern for NFL coaches this week might be players celebrating touchdowns with backflips and front-flips. Upcoming York Giants running back Cam Skattebo and Detroit Lions receiver Jameson Williams each went airborne in their Week 11 games, surely making their head coaches cringe. Teams have seven more weeks to keep their players on the ground.

    Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 11.

    In a recent development, after missing nearly a year with tears to his ACL and meniscus, Micah Parsons is set to return to the Packers' defensive line this week. The star linebacker has reportedly been cleared to play as of Monday, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

    Parsons reportedly needed one final clearance on his knee before getting the green light, and will now make his debut against the Rams on Wednesday.

    New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome will be sidelined for "multiple weeks" with a high ankle sprain, head coach John Harbaugh confirmed on Monday.

    It's still unclear if Newsome will need surgery or if he will land on injured reserve, which would knock him out for at least four games.

    "It's a serious high ankle. It's gonna be one of those lengthy high ankles," Harbaugh mentioned, via ESPN. "It's going to be multiple weeks.".

    For more on Newsome's injury, click here.

    San Francisco is finally parting ways with wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk.

    In a recent development, after a months-long saga around the receiver wanting to be released, Aiyuk was officially waived by the 49ers on Monday. That confirms reports earlier on Monday indicating that Aiyuk would finally be released.

    Other teams will have until Wednesday to claim Aiyuk, who will become a free agent after he clears waivers.

    Former Colts quarterback Daniel Jones was not claimed on Monday, thus making him a free agent.

    Jones is free to sign with any team that wants him, and that team can pay him the veteran minimum.

    The Colts still owe Jones about $20 million.

    The Commanders have activated running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt from injured reserve, and he is off the injury report.

    Recent findings suggest that JCM will play Monday night against the Bengals. He hasn't played since Week 5 due to a groin injury.

    So far this season, Croskey-Merritt has 239 yards and two touchdowns on 67 carries. He also has 40 yards on five receptions.

    The Cardinals have reportedly fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

    It has been revealed that arizona's defense has allowed 355.2 yards per game this season, the seventh-most in the league. The Cardinals' allowing 29.4 points per game is the second-most in the league, trailing only the Raiders at 29.7 points per game.

    San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch has agreed to a multi-year contract extension with the team, according to reports.

    Lynch and team owner Jed York agreed to the latest contract with a handshake while on the sideline at Estadio Banorte before Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, Fox Sports' Jay Glazer reported.

    Sources indicate that exact terms of Lynch's extension have not yet been reported. The 49ers have not officially declared the agreement. Lynch's current contract was set to expire after this season.

    Lynch's latest deal joins an extension for head coach Kyle Shanahan, who reached agreement on the contract in September shortly after the 49ers played the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia. San Francisco's international games this season have been extremely lucrative for the team's top football authority figures.

    Rams head coach Sean McVay said Monday that tight end Terrance Ferguson will need season-ending surgery on his ankle.

    Ferguson is the latest Rams player to be dealing with a long-term injury. Wide receiver Puka Nacua will also miss the remainder of the season due to a knee injury. Davante Adams has been sidelined since Week 6, though he is expected back by mid-December.

    It has been revealed that ferguson's season ends with him playing in just three games. He finished with 63 yards and a touchdown on seven receptions.

    The San Francisco 49ers are reportedly releasing veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.

    Aiyuk missed the entire 2025 NFL season after recovering from a knee injury he suffered in 2024, just months after signing a four-year, $120 million extension with the team. He suffered a torn ACL and MCL in late October 2024 and hasn't played a snap in the league since.

    After being placed on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list to start the year, reports later emerged that Aiyuk failed to participate in team meetings, and the Niners were frustrated with the "lack of communication." Eventually, he was placed on the Reserve/Left Squad list in December due to his continued absence and lack of communication with the team.

    If the Fresh England Patriots are interested in adding quarterback Daniel Jones, head coach Mike Vrabel isn't saying so.

    According to recent reports, while Jones waits to clear waivers, the Patriots named Tommy DeVito as their starting QB for Week 12's matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers. However, even if New England signed Jones, he would be unlikely to take the field with them so soon after joining the team.

    Taking over after Drake Maye was injured in Week 10's game versus the Detroit Lions, DeVito completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards with 1 touchdown and 1 interception.

    "We're excited about that, good preseason, and Tommy's improved," Vrabel remarked at his Monday press conference.

    According to recent reports, "I know that going into the last game, I think that being thrown in there and had some good plays, had some things that he can improve on and little things," he added. "I think that was probably the biggest thing is just saying, 'Hey, getting back into game action. How do you work in the pocket?' These are things that he got so much better on when he got here.".

    Green Bay Packers linebacker Micah Parsons "did well" in Sunday's padded practice session, according to coach Matt LaFleur.

    However, the team will wait until after Tuesday's practice to determine if Parsons can play in Wednesday's matchup with the Los Angeles Rams.

    The status of offensive lineman Sean Rhyan (high ankle sprain) and linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) are also still to be determined. Rhyan has been out since Week 7, while Franklin has been sidelined since Week 6.

    Running back Josh Jacobs (fractured finger) is unlikely to play Wednesday, but is doing individual drills to maintain conditioning, LaFleur said.

    Fernando Mendoza's first career NFL touchdown pass is now in the books.

    Recent findings suggest that the Las Vegas Raiders quarterback connected with running back Ashton Jeanty for a deep touchdown in the second quarter of their matchup with the Denver Broncos on Sunday afternoon. Mendoza found Jeanty open up the right side of the field for what ended up being an easy 68-yard score at Empower Field.

    The touchdown brought the Raiders within one touchdown of the Broncos just ahead of halftime.

    Naturally, Mendoza was extremely excited.

    Investors looking beyond the short-term noise and focusing on long-term returns can track top Wall Street analysts to pick the right stocks, backed by strong research.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    According to recent reports, this week's first stock pick is Datadog, an AI-powered observability and security platform. The manufacturer will announce its results for the third quarter on Nov. 4. Datadog is seeing strong demand for its offerings, thanks to cloud migration and rapid AI adoption. TipRanks' KPIs tool for DDOG indicates the growth in its customer base over the past few years amid increasing market penetration and growing adoption of its products.

    It has been revealed that heading into Q3 FY26 earnings, Bank of America analyst Koji Ikeda reiterated a buy rating on Datadog stock and raised his price target to $335 from $305. The analyst noted that industry checks and data indicate that infrastructure software demand is strengthening, with AI increasingly driving usage and growth.

    Ikeda called Datadog and Atlassian his top picks, saying that companies that can show that AI is a tailwind to growth could see their valuation rerate, even at premium multiples. He added that the total addressable market for observability is growing faster than anticipated, driven by accelerated growth of enterprise AI and the rapid ramp of consumer AI agents.

    The five-star analyst believes that focus will be on revenue growth, which he estimates to be 28.7% for Q3 FY26 versus the Street's consensus of 29.1%. Ikeda thinks that the market is underestimating the growth prospects of DDOG's security products. Meanwhile, he cautioned investors about concentration risk related to large customers.

    "We think results will be supportive of our long-term thesis that Datadog is a strong share gainer in the rapidly expanding observability opportunity," mentioned Ikeda.

    Industry observers note that while Nvidia's GTC Berlin offered no major updates, Moore noted the conference reflected that the manufacturer continues to add to its significant advantages heading into 2027. The analyst noted that Vera Rubin is gaining momentum, though details on next year's Rubin Ultra were lighter than expected.

    With demand outpacing supply, Moore mentioned that focus is on closing the gap. In this regard, he highlighted the supply chain deals on substrate, packaging and testing. While the analyst continues to view TSMC 3 nm wafer supply as the biggest challenge, he expects it to ease over time.

    Etihad’s Newly introduced Credit Cards Are Primarily for Status Chasers

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S.
    • The two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee).
    • According to recent reports, they also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two upcoming credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

    The two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

    According to recent reports, they also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

    Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

    The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    Sources indicate that 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    Welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for new applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    Elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

    You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

    The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    Sources indicate that 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    Sources indicate that 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

    According to recent reports, welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

    To maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

    Wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

    According to recent reports, travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

    The card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

    The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

    That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

    With the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in Latest York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

    According to recent reports, bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

    If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

    Industry observers note that however, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

    The earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

    That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

    Plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

    It has been revealed that those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.).

    Industry observers note that one of the most interesting perks of the fresh cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

    According to recent reports, there are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

    If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

    While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

    Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

    It has been revealed that you want a travel credit card that prioritizes what’s key to you. Here are some of the best travel credit cards of 2026:.

    Flexibility, point transfers and a large bonus: Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card.

    No annual fee: Wells Fargo Autograph® Card.

    Flat-rate travel rewards: Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card.

    Bonus travel rewards and high-end perks: Chase Sapphire Reserve®.

    Luxury perks: American Express Platinum Card®.

    Business travelers: Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card.

    #97081. Breaking: What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

    Breaking: What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (724 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car.
    • The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.
    • It has been revealed that A visual exterior inspection.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car. It’s intended to cover any costs the dealer incurs to make sure a used car is showroom-ready, from mechanical inspections to detailing.

    The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.

    It has been revealed that A visual exterior inspection. An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.

    Recent findings suggest that an interior inspection. The engine and auto interior are examined and tested, and any problems are documented.

    A test drive. The car is taken out for a drive to check that it runs well and that the radio, brakes, A/C and other components are all functioning properly.

    Sources indicate that service and repair. Any interior or exterior mechanical, functional or cosmetic issues that were found are repaired, including paint, dents, oil changes and major engine work.

    Inspection. Once repairs are completed, the car is inspected again to make sure everything looks and functions as it should.

    According to recent reports, detailing. This includes deep interior, engine and exterior cleaning as well as any necessary leather refurbishing, bumper repair or wheel restoration.

    Reconditioning fees are legal, but that doesn’t mean you have to pay them. Dealers can charge whatever they want for a reconditioning fee, and it’s not uncommon to find them ranging from around $500 to over $2,000.

    In a recent development, the good news: Reconditioning fees, like most dealer extras, can be negotiable. Ask the dealer for a breakdown of the reconditioning fee to see what kind of work was done to prepare the car for sale. If the work was minor but the fee is high — for example, if they’re asking for $1,995 but replaced the floor mats only — that’s a good sign it’s a bogus charge.

    Recent findings suggest that however, when it comes time for negotiation, don’t just haggle over the reconditioning fee or other individual fees. The best way to negotiate is to focus on the out-the-door price, or the total amount you’re paying for the car. This simplifies the negotiation process and keeps you focused on the true price of your car.

    All dealers invest some amount in reconditioning, but those costs are often built into the dealer’s asking price for a vehicle, rather than as a separate charge.

    Recent findings suggest that some dealers opt to add a reconditioning fee to the bill because it allows them to advertise a lower asking price online, which doesn’t include fees. It’s a tactic to get you into their dealership, since the asking price is lower than that of other dealerships.

    However, once you arrive, you may find that the out-the-door price is the same — or more — compared with what other dealers are asking.

    Industry observers note that some car-buying experts recommend avoiding dealerships that charge reconditioning fees altogether. But remember that the out-the-door price is what matters at the end of the day, so it’s worth comparing prices at multiple dealerships to find the best deal.

    Industry observers note that reddit is an online forum where users share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like car buying, so we sifted through Reddit threads to get a sense of how users feel about reconditioning fees. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

    It has been revealed that reddit users are generally skeptical toward reconditioning fees. Many users view these fees as a bait-and-switch tactic: dealers advertise an attractive price online and then tack on the fee at the dealership, inflating the actual out-the-door cost well above what was listed. Car buyers frequently share stories of being hit with reconditioning fees ranging from a few hundred dollars up to $2,000 or more, often with little or no evidence of what work was actually done.

    Car-buying experts on Reddit point out that most dealerships already build reconditioning costs into the sticker price, so if the fee is listed separately, the dealership may be double-dipping. Several users suggest that car buyers ask their dealer for an itemized breakdown of the work done, but most users recommend negotiating the total out-the-door price rather than individual fees.

    By David Jagielski, CPA – Nov 23, 2026 at 4:59PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.

    Although Warren Buffett no longer runs Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.49%)(BRKB +0.41%), the manufacturer still operates with the same investing principles, focusing its efforts on high-quality investments.

    In a recent development, at a time when the markets have been shaky of late, particularly pertaining to the tech sector, Berkshire has been a stock that's been rising in value lately. Could it be a safe place for investors to park their money, amid the uncertainty in not only tech but also the broader markets?

    Tech stocks have been doing well for the most part this year, as the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF has risen by around 13%, which is in line with Berkshire's performance -- it's up around 14%.

    In a recent development, but what's notable is the shift over the past three months. Berkshire's stock has risen by 16% during that stretch, while the Tech-focused ETF has gone in the opposite direction, falling by 11%. It could be a sign of investors pivoting to safer stocks, such as Berkshire, in the wake of all the turmoil involving tech of late.

    Berkshire is, after all, a prototypical value stock that doesn't take on much risk and which can provide investors with excellent value. However, under fresh CEO Greg Abel, I've noticed the manufacturer investing more in tech, including Bending Spoons, a serial acquirer I couldn't imagine Buffett investing in. But it is a minor position in the overall portfolio.

    By and large, Berkshire's focus remains unchanged, with close to half of its portfolio centered around three large, iconic companies: Apple, American Express, and Coca-Cola.

    With stalwarts such as those centering its portfolio, the stock can indeed be a safe option for investors. But whether it's the best option is certainly debatable.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    There are a couple of reasons I wouldn't buy Berkshire's stock for safety. The first is that it doesn't pay a dividend, which can be crucial when investors want to maximize returns amid uncertainty. The second is that at 16 times earnings, the stock is a bit more expensive than normal.

    Industry observers note that ultimately, with markets in a bit of a downturn of late, I think investors can find better options, such as discounted dividend stocks that at least offer decent yields. Berkshire can be a good safe-haven investment, but before buying the stock, investors may want to consider other options.
