    #97077. Ground Truth: The Unsung Foundation Of Industrial Autonomy

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (967 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Ground Truth: The Unsung Foundation Of Industrial Autonomy

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (967 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ronald Bisio is Group President, Field Systems, at Trimble.
    • ​While the public’s attention is captivated by self-driving vehicles, city robotaxis and visions of flying cars, there’s a more consequential autonomous evolution taking place across heavy industry.
    • Recent findings suggest that in building and infrastructure construction, autonomy is a navigation and execution challenge.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ronald Bisio is Group President, Field Systems, at Trimble.

    ​While the public’s attention is captivated by self-driving vehicles, city robotaxis and visions of flying cars, there’s a more consequential autonomous evolution taking place across heavy industry.

    Recent findings suggest that in building and infrastructure construction, autonomy is a navigation and execution challenge. A 50-ton excavator doesn’t just travel across a construction site from Point A to Point B. It digs trenches, grades slopes and moves thousands of tons of earth to match a complex 3D digital model down to the centimeter. A commercial freight truck hauling 80,000 pounds along a highway corridor isn’t just following traffic. With advanced digital mapping and precise positioning technologies, the truck holds a precise spatial line through torrential rain, dense fog or featureless stretches of road where cameras lose contrast.

    In a recent development, ​In the physical world, knowing what’s immediately around a machine is critical, but a real breakthrough happens when we connect local perception through cameras, LiDAR and radar to spatial ground truth, an invisible infrastructure that complements onboard sensors. This is the high-precision global positioning that uses an absolute coordinate frame of latitude, longitude, elevation and time down to the centimeter. When we connect local perception with precise positioning, we close the gap between machinery observing what’s around and knowing exactly where the machinery sits on the physical earth.

    With these technological advances in heavy industry, there’s an understandable anxiety about automation replacing human workers. But as I visit customers and jobsites, I see the opposite. Across construction and transportation, the shortage of skilled workers is evident. Contractors can’t find enough experienced workers to meet infrastructure construction demands, and fleet owners are facing historically high driver turnover.

    Sources indicate that ​Fundamentally, industrial autonomy is about elevating human activity and decision making. By putting high-precision digital guidance into a cab, an inexperienced operator can perform complex grading work. Instead of performing repetitive manual layout, workers can oversee connected equipment, manage exceptions and focus on site safety. Autonomous equipment and robotics help automate repetitive and hazardous operations, freeing human talent to focus on higher-order tasks.

    It has been revealed that ​Over the past few years, perception sensors have improved dramatically. Cameras, LiDAR and radar give machines exceptional eye-level vision so they can recognize nearby obstacles, workers and vehicles.

    ​But vision sensors have two inherent vulnerabilities. First, these optical systems may degrade in harsh environments and be rendered momentarily blind by factors like heavy dust, glare or dark tunnels. Second, vision sensors lack global context. A camera can spot an obstacle five feet away, but it can’t tell a bulldozer where it sits on the earth’s surface.​.

    According to recent reports, to address this, machines may rely on satellite positioning, but they also must be on guard for the illusion of precision. Driven by the rise of low-cost radios, increasing radio frequency interference leaves satellite signals vulnerable to both accidental jamming and deliberate spoofing. Spoofing is particularly dangerous because a legacy GPS receiver may lock onto a falsified signal and output a position with high mathematical confidence, even though the machine is actually several meters off target.

    Sources indicate that ​If a mapping app gets bad location data, a passenger vehicle driver might make a wrong turn or miss an exit. But when heavy equipment is shaping a foundation or grading a road, inaccurate location data may cause costly rework, wasted materials and safety risks.

    In a recent development, rather than jumping straight to driverless machines on jobsites, we’re seeing a steady advancement of smart equipment guidance and operator assistance. Recent milestones in the field demonstrate the impact:​.

    In the recent building of a latest EV manufacturing facility, Landmark Construction, a civil contractor utilizing our positioning solutions, orchestrated more than 150 machine-guided excavators, dozers and graders connected to a single 3D digital site blueprint. Guided by continuous satellite positioning, the machines automatically adjusted blades and buckets to match design lines. By eliminating six or seven manual data transfer steps between the field and the office, earthmoving tasks that previously took a month were completed in several days—and often with more accuracy.

    High-precision positioning is steadily moving out of specialized niches and into mainstream production of electric vehicles and commercial long-haul trucks. Fusing satellite data with vehicle movement sensors allows passenger cars and substantial trucks to maintain lane-level accuracy in urban canyons and bad weather, giving automated driver-assist systems the required reliability.

    In the air, autonomous drones are opening up new options for delivering urgent medical supplies. Guided by resilient positioning technology, these delivery drones can maintain their flight accuracy and operate safely despite localized signal degradation, bad weather and magnetic interference.

    Technology leaders considering autonomous solutions for their operations should keep these three principles in mind:.

    It has been revealed that 1. Precision is the bridge to physical reality. A few inches of spatial error may not matter in the virtual world, but on active jobsites, centimeter-level precision is what’s needed for accurate physical execution on the first pass.

    According to recent reports, 2. Spatial trust is necessary for safe autonomy. Heavy machinery can’t alter the physical world without verified, uncompromised positioning. Precision is the core safety architecture for real-world automation.

    It has been revealed that 3. Accuracy amplifies human potential. High-precision guidance elevates rather than replaces human judgment. Precision technology takes guesswork out of complex physical tasks so less experienced workers can operate like skilled veterans.

    In a recent development, ​Industrial autonomy aims to seamlessly connect digital design and physical reality. A backbone of high-precision positioning opens up new possibilities for pairing intelligent machinery with human expertise. We only need to dream them into reality.

    Latest Update: What Are Repositioning Cruises?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another.
    • Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.
    • Sources indicate that because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

    Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

    Sources indicate that because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

    One key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

    This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

    It has been revealed that another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

    According to recent reports, just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a new region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

    Repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit key sites when off the ship.

    It has been revealed that if there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

    Industry observers note that for ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy highlights, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

    According to recent reports, many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

    According to recent reports, if you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

    Sources indicate that you can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

    Keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

    Here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

    It has been revealed that this journey repositions the ship from Miami, where it sails on Caribbean itineraries, to Seattle, where it will visit ports in Alaska during the spring and summer months. Departing April 8, 2027, the 18-night cruise includes stops at various ports in Colombia, Panama and Mexico, as well as San Diego and Los Angeles, before arriving in Seattle on April 26.

    Regent Seven Seas Cruises' all-suite luxury ship Seven Seas Mariner will sail between Fresh York and Lisbon, making stops in Canada, Morocco and the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores.

    Departing April 29, 2027, the 16-night journey ends in Lisbon, Portugal, as the ship repositions to Europe, where it will sail various itineraries, including Mediterranean sailings later in the summer season.

    Recent findings suggest that departing Seattle on Sept. 28, 2027, Norwegian Jade will sail to Yokohama, Japan, with stops in Alaska and northern Japan. This is a way to travel across the Pacific with less jet lag, since the journey takes place over several days, with ship clocks typically adjusted gradually (often an hour at a time) during the sailing. Note that the voyage also crosses the International Date Line.

    If Greenland has been on your bucket list, this 16-night sailing is a way to get up close and personal with its natural scenery. Departing Reykjavik on Aug. 25, 2027, Azamara Quest will sail from Iceland to the U.S. It will make stops in Greenland, Canada and Latest England before reaching the Big Apple.

    Departing Bergen, Norway, on June 11, 2027, this 28-night sailing aboard Viking Vela sails around Iceland's coast, makes two stops in Greenland and crosses the Atlantic before reaching New York.

    #97070. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh Just Laid Out 3 Scenarios for "Super Intelligence." 2 of Them Are "Less Positive," Including 1 Scenario That Outright Disappoints

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (844 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Fed Chair Kevin Warsh Just Laid Out 3 Scenarios for "Super Intelligence." 2 of Them Are "Less Positive," Including 1 Scenario That Outright Disappoints

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (844 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As chair of the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors, Kevin Warsh has a powerful job.
    • That's why his thinking on artificial intelligence, or what Warsh refers to as “super intelligence,” matters.
    • 16, at a conference for the Fed's Productivity and Jobs Task Force hosted by the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Warsh stated the Fed is modeling three possible paths for the economy as AI continues to develop.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Bram Berkowitz – Nov 23, 2026 at 5:00PM EST.

    As chair of the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors, Kevin Warsh has a powerful job. His words can move markets, and his view of the economy can play a substantial role in shaping the policy decisions that follow.

    That's why his thinking on artificial intelligence, or what Warsh refers to as “super intelligence,” matters. Super intelligence (SI) is the term adopted by President Donald Trump and his administration to describe AI, and has become a driving force of both corporate spending and stock market gains. Whether it delivers on its promise could impact growth, jobs, and inflation for years. These are the very concerns the Fed is charged with managing, so it has to try to figure out what's coming before it arrives.

    On Nov. 16, at a conference for the Fed's Productivity and Jobs Task Force hosted by the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Warsh stated the Fed is modeling three possible paths for the economy as AI continues to develop.

    Two of these scenarios are "less positive," including one where artificial intelligence outright disappoints.

    Image source: Official Federal Reserve Photo.

    During his opening remarks, Warsh said Fed staff had built three illustrative scenarios over the next several years, stressing that they are not forecasts and that he was not there to offer predictions.

    The first is the one that every investor hopes for. Productivity rises, and the gains are shared evenly between workers and those who manage and own capital. In this scenario, growth remains above its long-run average, and the economy remains near full employment.

    The second scenario is interesting because it doesn't require artificial intelligence to fail. It requires it to work.

    According to recent reports, "An SI-driven expansion could bring substantial labor market disruption as some jobs are displaced, rather than complemented, by technology," Warsh remarked. "GDP growth would still rise above its long-term average. But widespread automation, combined with labor market frictions, could push the jobless rate above levels consistent with full employment.".

    The third is a letdown, where "SI could disappoint." After heavy investment and the strong market rally we've seen, returns on capital are lower than expected, a concern some investors already share. This leads to a decline in valuations, and the economy slows before eventually recovering without the productivity gains.

    Industry observers note that again, these aren't predictions from Warsh, who has tried to avoid any kind of forward guidance since becoming chair. Warsh also noted, "many other outcomes -- probably including one that will prove most accurate -- could be drawn.".

    It has been revealed that still, if the Fed is beginning to model these three scenarios, it's likely at least somewhat on the minds of Warsh and the rest of the Fed's board. Interestingly, the first and third scenarios are easier to understand because they are more black-and-white. Either AI works, benefiting the economy, or it doesn't, and the economy and likely the stock market struggle.

    But it's the second that I find most interesting, and likely the one most investors are not factoring in.

    A successful AI boom that leaves workers behind is harder to see coming and likely harder to model. It's also one that could make it difficult for the Fed to manage its two goals of stable prices and maximum employment, because this scenario could push them in different directions.

    In a recent development, if AI delivers on its promise, companies will use it to do more with fewer people. This would lift margins and productivity in the near term, which is exactly what bulls are counting on, and may already be happening this year.

    Sources indicate that but the people who lose their jobs or are forced to switch to lower-paying jobs are also consumers. Consumer spending accounts for more than two-thirds of the U.S. economy.

    According to recent reports, fewer or lower paychecks, or less confidence in keeping them, means less spending power. Over time, that could hit the revenue of the same companies that saved money by cutting costs.

    AI investment is already a major source of growth. Business equipment spending jumped nearly 21% in the third quarter, helping lift GDP growth to 3.4%, according to Reuters. But this doesn't replace the spending of millions of households.

    Nobody knows what will happen. Everything may work out, but investors should remember that forecasts rarely pan out as expected. The best case for AI isn't necessarily the best case for the consumers who power the economy.

    Long-term investors should remain invested, but it's vital to consider these scenarios and make sure your portfolio is prepared.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Lawrence Rothman, CFA – Updated Nov 23, 2026 at 5:11PM EST.
    • Recent findings suggest that when market volatility rises, many investors turn toward large and established companies for stability.
    • Recent findings suggest that colgate-Palmolive focuses on essential household items like toothpaste and soap, offering stability through products people buy regardless of the economy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Lawrence Rothman, CFA – Updated Nov 23, 2026 at 5:11PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Colgate-Palmolive ›.

    Recent findings suggest that when market volatility rises, many investors turn toward large and established companies for stability. Choosing between Colgate-Palmolive (CL -0.79%) and McDonald's (MCD +1.15%) requires weighing a household goods leader against a global fast-food powerhouse.

    Recent findings suggest that colgate-Palmolive focuses on essential household items like toothpaste and soap, offering stability through products people buy regardless of the economy. McDonald's dominates the quick-service restaurant industry by leveraging a massive franchise network that generates recurring rent and royalty income. While one provides daily necessities and the other offers affordable convenience, both represent mature businesses that investors often compare for long-term consistency.

    Sources indicate that colgate-Palmolive operates as a global leader in segments like oral care, home care, and pet nutrition through brands such as Colgate and Hill's. These essential products are sold in over 200 countries, making the company a prominent name among consumer staples stocks. Investors should note that nearly 11% of its 2025 sales came from Walmart (WMT +1.27%), creating a customer concentration that gives the retailer significant bargaining power over trade discounts.

    According to recent reports, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, revenue reached $21.3 billion, which represents a growth rate of approximately 5.9% compared to the prior 12-month period. The firm reported net income of $2.2 billion during this same period as it navigated a complex global environment. This performance reflects top-line expansion across its various geographic regions even as it faces competition from smaller, digital-first brands.

    McDonald's utilizes a franchise-heavy business model where roughly 95% of its 45,000 restaurants are managed by independent owners. These franchisees provide the company with steady streams of rent and royalties, which support a high net margin.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, revenue reached $27.8 billion, representing a growth rate of roughly 5.8% over the previous 12-month period. The company recorded net income of $9.0 billion. McDonald's reported a net margin of 32.4% during this time frame, illustrating the profitability inherent in its franchise-led structure.

    Colgate-Palmolive faces significant risks from its global footprint, as geopolitical instability in regions like the Middle East can disrupt operations. The tech giant also deals with intense competition from private labels. Additionally, evolving global regulations concerning environmental impact and product safety require ongoing investment to ensure compliance.

    Recent findings suggest that mcDonald's depends on the financial health of its franchisees to execute its expansion plans, and any broad economic downturn could impact its royalty streams. The business is also susceptible to reputational damage from food safety incidents and recent class action lawsuits regarding product labeling and marketing claims.

    McDonald's carries a lower Forward P/E, while Colgate-Palmolive appears more attractive based on its P/S ratio, which compares market value to sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    While neither company is a fast grower, they have generated positive sales and earnings gains. That's positive for mature companies.

    It has been revealed that additionally, both have made strong commitments to paying dividends to shareholders. That's an notable component of their total returns. In fact, Colgate and McDonald's have increased payments annually for 63 and 50 straight years, respectively. That makes them Dividend Kings, or companies that have raised dividends for at least 50 consecutive years.

    In a recent development, both have sufficient earnings to support dividends, too. Colgate-Palmolive has a payout ratio, or dividends divided by earnings, of 82%. Meanwhile, McDonald's has a 59% payout ratio.

    Turning to the dividend yields. McDonald's 2.8% yield surpasses Colgate's 2.2% yield.

    Recent findings suggest that the decision comes down to the underlying businesses and dividends. With McDonald's higher dividend yield and asset-light business conducive to free cash flow generation, that stock is my choice over Colgate-Palmolive.

    #97055. Cybersecurity Practices That Can Create A False Sense Of Security

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1304 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Cybersecurity Practices That Can Create A False Sense Of Security

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1304 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Organizations invest significant time and resources in cybersecurity measures designed to protect their systems, data and operations.
    • Sources indicate that for tech leaders, the challenge is recognizing when established security practices are effectively reducing risk and when they may be simply creating the appearance of preparedness.
    • According to recent reports, “We have 24/7 monitoring” is not the same as, “We will catch an matter at 2 a.m.” This is truly a false sense of security unless your teams have fine-tuned alerts very well over time for your situations and context.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Organizations invest significant time and resources in cybersecurity measures designed to protect their systems, data and operations. However, even practices that seem responsible can create a false sense of security—especially when they’re treated as substitutes for more comprehensive protection and ongoing risk assessment.

    Sources indicate that for tech leaders, the challenge is recognizing when established security practices are effectively reducing risk and when they may be simply creating the appearance of preparedness. Here, Forbes Technology Council members highlight common cybersecurity practices and beliefs that can give organizations misplaced confidence and explain what to do instead.

    According to recent reports, “We have 24/7 monitoring” is not the same as, “We will catch an matter at 2 a.m.” This is truly a false sense of security unless your teams have fine-tuned alerts very well over time for your situations and context. That means TP/FP are identified, and actual signals are not lost in the high-volume alert noise. To test, inject a true alert at an inconvenient hour and see if ops is detecting it and acting upon it. Monitoring is mostly a comfort unless you make it a security control. - Pradeep Sandhu, Cywarden, Inc.

    Industry observers note that the fundamental assumption behind traditional cybersecurity is that all the technology in your security stack will behave exactly as designed, requiring little oversight. This could not be further from the truth. Constant governance and visibility into your security system is no longer an option. It is a necessity that can’t be overlooked or underestimated, and it’s a critical issue that must be addressed, especially as we navigate the uncharted territory of AI. - Kevin Lynch, Optiv.

    Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    Prioritizing security by a generic risk model describes the average organization, which does not exist. One bank had 362 vulnerabilities under attack in its network that global data never saw. A score trained on everyone is a statement about no one. - Michael Roytman, Empirical Security.

    Industry observers note that as a CISO, I’ve sat through HiTrust, SOC 2 and PCI audits, and I value them. But a clean report is a snapshot of scoped controls and evidence chosen for an auditor to see, not proof we’d stop a real attacker. The danger is when “we passed” becomes the finish line and the board sees a green light. I treat audits as the floor, then measure what matters: real prevention, detection and remediation speed. - Lane Sullivan, Concentric AI.

    Many organizations mistake end-to-end encryption for security. Encryption answers one question: Can someone read the message in transit? It states nothing about who is on the other end or whether a record survives. Further, the same encryption that keeps attackers out can end up keeping the firm out, too. Security means governing the conversation at the source, with verified identities, managed access and a record the firm owns and can act on. - Dima Gutzeit, LeapXpert.

    According to recent reports, treating an approved business application as permanently trusted can create unchecked risk. Vendors now add AI agents and automation to software enterprises already use, giving new capabilities access to existing data, permissions and workflows. Security teams need to reassess what those applications can do as features change, not rely on the risk profile established when they were procured. - Ofer Klein, Reco.

    Software from an approved vendor, known repository, signed package or internal developer can still contain malicious or unintended behavior. Source and provenance are crucial, but they do not show what the finished code will actually do. Organizations should verify behavior before execution, not inherit trust from where the code came from. - Ken Ammon, CodeHunter.

    Recent findings suggest that early in my career, the problem was, “We don’t know what we have.” Today, most teams have dashboards full of alerts and findings, but visibility doesn’t equal security. If the data from your environment is not contextualized into actionable, cross-domain insights and proactive remediation workflows, you’ve just documented your exposure in more detail rather than successfully mitigating it. - Sivan Tehila, Onyxia Cyber.

    It has been revealed that A common misconception is that if an email passes through a security gateway, it must be safe. While traditional gateways catch known threats, they’re less effective against AI-driven attacks that don’t rely on malicious links or attachments. These newer attacks look and sound legitimate, making them harder to spot. That’s why organizations must pay attention to communication patterns. - Eyal Benishti, IRONSCALES.

    A green dashboard does not truly mean your business is secure. No alerts may signal gaps in visibility, not an absence of threats. Organizations need security that connects signals across their environment, backed by experts who monitor, investigate and respond 24/7. Regularly test your defenses to confirm teams can detect suspicious activity and act rapidly to contain threats before they do harm. - Neal Bradbury, Barracuda.

    One of the biggest misconceptions about open-source security is that finding vulnerabilities means you’re securing your software. Scanners and AI agents can flag thousands of risks, but without a clear remediation path, they create backlogs instead of protection. For end-of-life open-source software, the stakes are even higher. When official patches stop, vulnerabilities don’t. - Aaron Mitchell, HeroDevs.

    A dangerous belief is that more security tools automatically mean better security. In reality, too many disconnected tools can create blind spots, duplicate alerts and unclear ownership. A mature security posture is not defined by how much technology has been purchased but by how quickly the organization can detect, understand and contain a real threat. - Dr. Chiranjiv Roy, C5i.ai.

    In a recent development, vendor security questionnaires feel thorough, but they capture a one-time self-assessment from direct suppliers and say little about the vendors behind them. Risk changes constantly and often sits several tiers deep, so treat these questionnaires as a starting point, then pair them with continuous monitoring of the extended sub-tier supplier network for proactive supplier risk mitigation. - Yardley Pohl, interos.ai.

    It has been revealed that poorly executed phishing tests can do far more to damage employee trust than they will ever benefit an organization’s cybersecurity capability. Activities that penalize individuals, don’t result in meaningful and engaged education, or become so frequent that they annoy and create resentment do little to strengthen your cyber defenses. - Kim Bozzella, Protiviti.

    I think relying too heavily on periodic security audits can create a false sense of confidence. They’re valuable, but technology changes promptly, especially as teams introduce latest tools and AI into their workflows. I’ve learned that it’s important to keep reviewing how systems are actually being used, who has access and where new risks may be developing between audits. - Deniz Gezgin, Eightpoint.

    Mandatory password rotation is often mistaken for effective cybersecurity. Requiring employees to change passwords every 60 to 90 days can encourage predictable variations and credential reuse, potentially increasing security risks. Organizations should prioritize phishing-resistant multifactor authentication, compromised-credential detection and risk-based access controls over routine password expiration. - Gouri Sankar Dash, Tata Consultancy Services.

    Treating successful backups as proof of recovery can create false confidence. A backup job can finish successfully while a full restoration still fails or takes too long. Test recovery of a complete business workflow in an isolated environment, including its dependencies, and measure the time until people can actually use it. - Shahen Minasyan, Twin Peaks Inc. (TPI).

    Access and authentication controls are paramount to any internal system, but with AI agents now working alongside humans, impersonation is becoming a growing threat. These tools often rely on being able to access the same files and systems you can access. It may be productive, but left unattended, it’s risky. Building in systemic limitations to what AI agents can do on your behalf is an notable consideration. - Matt Wielbut, Openly.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    Recent findings suggest that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively latest corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    It has been revealed that the growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    It has been revealed that securitize reinforced "certain areas of the firm like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo remarked. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The organization posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo mentioned.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Johnny Rice – Nov 23, 2026 at 5:20PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he personally lobbied Nvidia's (NASDAQ: NVDA) board to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO, telling the network's Eamon Javers this morning that he had spoken with the board "directly and indirectly" in recent days and that he "convinced them" to reinstate Huang, who "did nothing wrong.".

    The crux of the matter seemed to be the national security concerns surrounding Huang's original departure: "They did ask for assurance on the national security threat," The President noted, "And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot.".

    The board's official announcement this morning echoed Trump's statements: "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk.".

    While the announcement led to a massive rally today -- Nvidia stock finished up 31% -- the President's involvement could have unintended consequences for shareholders.

    The national security concern stems from Huang's reported affair with Alice Huang, the former CEO of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer accused of contravening U.S. export controls. Ms. Huang is herself a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, though Beijing denies the espionage allegation. The Justice Department is investigating Megaspeed, so too is Nvidia, which opened its own investigation on Nov. 8. The board stated it has no reason to believe anyone had compromised tech giant secrets or U.S. national security.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    According to Trump, Attorney General Todd Blanche told him the government "does not possess evidence that [Huang] has engaged in any unlawful conduct" and that there's no reason to believe Huang poses a threat to national security.

    It has been revealed that trump told CNBC that not only is he not a threat, but that through his work, he is an invaluable asset: "People say, is it a threat to have him? No, it's a threat to lose him.".

    Trump cheered his reinstatement, saying: "I'm very, very happy that the tech giant had the courage and the board had the courage to do the right thing, and they suffered for two weeks, and the company suffered greatly.".

    Given the sensitive nature of all of this, the dramatic reversal of the board's decision would likely have raised eyebrows in Washington under any circumstance. But now that the President himself has claimed that his involvement was instrumental in changing the board's minds, I would expect serious scrutiny from Congress.

    Jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images.

    Legislators on both sides of the aisle expressed their skepticism. Republican Senator John Cornyn remarked on the social media platform X, "No national security risk? Based on what?" while Democratic Representative Jim Himes said in a statement that "Congress still has questions that require answers.".

    If any evidence of wrongdoing surfaces and Huang is forced out once more, I think the market's reaction will be even stronger on the way down.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, anthropic (ANT -1.43%) is officially a publicly traded company.
    • Many investors are interested in Anthropic as an IPO investment given its massive growth potential and the disruptive nature of artificial intelligence (AI).
    • We have abundant data on IPO stock performance dating back decades, which has allowed researchers to analyze them closely.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Brett Schafer – Nov 23, 2026 at 5:23PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    In a recent development, anthropic (ANT -1.43%) is officially a publicly traded company. The company sold shares at $83 this week, which then popped to over $100 on the first day of trading before falling back to earth and closing at roughly $89 on Friday, Nov. 21. It is now the 14th-largest company in the world by market cap, worth $1.16 trillion.

    Many investors are interested in Anthropic as an IPO investment given its massive growth potential and the disruptive nature of artificial intelligence (AI). But what does the data say about investing in IPOs near their debut? The answer is clear: Investors should exercise patience with this smoking-hot stock. Here's why.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    We have abundant data on IPO stock performance dating back decades, which has allowed researchers to analyze them closely. When looking three years out from the IPO date -- which is what long-term investors should be doing for buy-and-hold portfolios -- 64% of IPO stocks underperformed, while 29% beat the market averages. However, a lot of the time, even stocks with market-beating performance experienced a post-IPO slump. This usually provides investors with potential buying opportunities at lower prices if they are patient enough to wait six months after listing.

    Sources indicate that there are two main reasons for this, regardless of tech giant quality. First, an IPO is generally considered a time for insiders to sell some or all of their positions, not to buy. A venture capital firm, a vice president, or an entry-level employee may now hold millions in Anthropic stock. It is not shocking, then, to see them sell some of their stakes now that the stock is publicly traded, a practice usually done in increments during the lockup period after the IPO. Second, a company and Wall Street generally want to maximize the IPO price at which they sell shares, which can, on average, lead to elevated valuations for investors buying in the early weeks of trading.

    Taking all this into consideration, it is no surprise that the average IPO stock performs poorly over the next three years.

    Seeing this data, a smart investor looking to buy shares of Anthropic will wait at least a few months before starting a position, which will (on average) lead to a better entry point.

    According to recent reports, the next question is whether Anthropic is a high-quality business in the first place. Growth has been on fire leading up to the IPO, with trailing revenue now at $35 billion at the end of the third quarter, up from less than $5 billion in 2025. This is an incredible level of growth, as enterprises and individuals alike spend gobs of money on Claude's coding tools and other automations.

    In a recent development, growth should continue in the years ahead, but don't think the AI race is over. Anthropic has many competitors, both large and small, and has to contend with open-source AI models that enterprises are increasingly adopting to lower costs. The question is whether Anthropic has locked in enterprise customers to its AI tools, creating switching costs, or whether enterprises will eventually move to cheaper solutions.

    In a recent development, profit margins are also a major question. Right now, Anthropic is generating around break-even profitability. However, it is about to embark on a spending spree to build its own AI data centers, amid the general volatility of the AI race. A year ago, many thought Anthropic was well behind OpenAI, its main competitor. Who's to say what its competitive position will be like a year from now?

    It has been revealed that I wouldn't fault anyone looking to get in on Anthropic. This is one of the fastest-growing companies in history, with a product that is indistinguishable from magic. There are certainly risks to the investment, but Anthropic also may be the largest firm in the world 10 years from now.

    Sources indicate that anyone looking to buy shares should hold off in the first weeks of trading, if not longer. Let the company get through its insider sales post any lock-up periods, which end in May of next year, before starting to build a position. On average, you will find a better trading price in doing so.

    10 stocks we like better than SK Hynix ›.

    Sources indicate that shares of SK Hynix (SKHY +20.00%) charged sharply higher on Wednesday, jumping as much as 23.7%. By the time the market closed, the stock was still up 20%.

    The catalyst that sent the semiconductor specialist higher was news of a high-profile potential suitor.

    Recent findings suggest that SK Hynix was reportedly the subject of takeover interest from Japanese investment holding organization and tech conglomerate SoftBank Group (SFTBY +19.27%). Chairman Masayoshi Son approached numerous Wall Street banks to discuss financing options to acquire the chipmaker for $1 trillion, according to a report that first appeared in The Information. The price under consideration would have been roughly 1.7 times SK Hynix's market cap of $576 billion as of Friday's market close.

    The sheer magnitude of the offer and the potential national security implications were just a few of the obstacles that reportedly scuttled the deal, though it isn't clear whether a formal offer was ever tendered.

    According to recent reports, softBank has made no secret of its ambition to achieve end-to-end control over all elements of the artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductor supply chain. The tech giant already owns data center chip designer Ampere Computing and power infrastructure specialist SB Energy, as well as an 86% controlling stake in chip designer Arm Holdings. SoftBank also holds a position in AI start-up OpenAI.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    According to recent reports, bringing SK Hynix into the fold would have given the firm a direct pipeline to DRAM, NAND flash, and high-bandwidth memory (HBM). However, in a statement, it stated, "SoftBank explores many opportunities, and this one is no longer under active consideration." The wording suggests the deal was, in fact, explored.

    So is SK Hynix worth $1 trillion? It's doubtful. A premium of that magnitude would likely have drawn the ire of smaller SoftBank investors, even as Son holds a dominant 33% stake in the company. Moreover, as Korea's dominant maker of HBM, it's unlikely the deal would have passed regulatory muster.

    At less than 7 times earnings, SK Hynix stock appears attractively priced. However, the historical boom-and-bust cycle has some investors concerned, and the jury is still out on whether the firm can maintain its juicy profit margins while the future of AI plays out.

    Parsons had 12.5 sacks in his 14 games with the Packers last season, and had accounted for a third of Green Bay's pressures before he went down. It was his first campaign with the team after they acquired him in a deal with the Dallas Cowboys just ahead of Week 1.

"I'll be looking forward to returning to the field.".

    Sources indicate that the Packers will enter Wednesday with a 6-4 record, which has them in last in the NFC North but very much alive in the playoff conversation. They were off last week, but went into their bye fresh off a rough 30-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

    Industry observers note that while it's been almost a full year since he's played in a game, Parsons is more than ready to get back. And he's well aware of what a win over the Rams would do for the Packers' postseason hopes entering the final stretch of the season.

    "I'm really geeked up," he mentioned, via ESPN's Rob Demovsky. "They're like, 'Are you nervous?' I'm just so focused, I'm so locked in on what's ahead of me.     Retirees: Is Now the Time to Ditch S&P 500 Funds?

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By David Jagielski, CPA – Nov 23, 2026 at 6:13PM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ›.
    • Industry observers note that the stock market has been volatile in recent weeks, with the scandal involving Nvidia and its CEO, Jensen Huang, resigning and then coming back within a few weeks, highlighting just how erratic tracking the S&P 500 can be.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By David Jagielski, CPA – Nov 23, 2026 at 6:13PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ›.

    Industry observers note that the stock market has been volatile in recent weeks, with the scandal involving Nvidia and its CEO, Jensen Huang, resigning and then coming back within a few weeks, highlighting just how erratic tracking the S&P 500 can be. Last week, amid the Nvidia sell-off, the broad index fell to below 7,000 -- its lowest point since April. Now, with Nvidia's stock jumping on the news of Huang being reinstated as CEO, the index added more than 300 points in a single day.

    Industry observers note that the wild swings due to tech are something investors have to come to terms with if they track the index via funds such as the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO +4.46%). While over the long run it can be a good way to invest in the markets, the exposure the index has to tech these days makes it a riskier-than-normal option.

    For risk-averse investors and retirees, it begs the question: is investing in S&P 500 index funds still a good move right now?

    Through the S&P 500, investors gain access to the largest, most valuable companies on U.S. markets. But these days, that means a lot of tech exposure, as it's been tech stocks that have been rising feverishly due to artificial intelligence (AI) in recent years.

    Sources indicate that nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet are the largest holdings in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF. Just those five holdings alone account for close to 30% of the Vanguard S&P 500's portfolio. And that's just among the largest holdings. There are also many companies that indirectly have significant exposure to AI, including energy companies involved in data center build-outs.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    It has been revealed that tracking the S&P 500 makes sense for the long haul. But during a period of five years or less, a lot can happen. If a crash occurs, it can take a long time for the market to recover, time that retirees can't spare.

    For most long-term investors, tracking the S&P 500 still makes a lot of sense, even if there might be a potential crash or correction on the horizon.

    Retirees, however, may be better off considering dividend-oriented funds to track instead, which don't have nearly as much exposure to tech. Some funds don't have any exposure at all. During shorter periods, those types of investments can offer much less volatility and be safer options to hang on to.

    #97027. What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (747 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (747 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
    • Industry observers note that huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the firm.
    • Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

    Industry observers note that huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the firm. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

    Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

    "Although we expect the organization to fulfill all of its previously confirmed commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate latest multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said in a note Thursday.

    The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

    In a recent development, tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

    On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    It has been revealed that tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

    Recent findings suggest that it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The manufacturer had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

    Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

    In a recent development, coreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

    It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, said CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

    "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he said.

    "However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

    CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

    "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my company every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he mentioned in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

    Bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any significant changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

    The real issue is just how much money the manufacturer will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

    Industry observers note that "Major companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he noted. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

    — CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

    Tech Report: Applied Digital Stock Surged 20% on a Hyperscaler Deal. What to Know About Its $41 Billion in Leases

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Applied Digital (APLD +20.28%) shares jumped as much as 31% on Monday after the company stated it signed a newly introduced 150-megawatt, 18-year lease with a "tier-one investment-grade hyperscaler." The company said the lease brings its contracted base-term revenue above $41 billion.
    • In a recent development, the jump came one trading day after Applied Digital hit its lowest close of the past year, $11.49 on Friday.
    • Sources indicate that applied Digital builds data centers and rents them to companies that need power and space for artificial intelligence computing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 23, 2026 at 6:37PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Applied Digital ›.

    Applied Digital (APLD +20.28%) shares jumped as much as 31% on Monday after the company stated it signed a newly introduced 150-megawatt, 18-year lease with a "tier-one investment-grade hyperscaler." The company said the lease brings its contracted base-term revenue above $41 billion. The stock ultimately gave back some of that gain but still closed up 20% at $13.82.

    In a recent development, the jump came one trading day after Applied Digital hit its lowest close of the past year, $11.49 on Friday. Even after Monday's gain, the stock sits 72% below its 52-week high of $49.65 on May 28, and it's down 44% this year.

    Sources indicate that applied Digital builds data centers and rents them to companies that need power and space for artificial intelligence computing. A lease of this kind is a promise of rent once a building is finished and handed over.

    The manufacturer's quarterly report filed Oct. 7, before Monday's lease, listed $35.7 billion in minimum contracted lease payments. Of that, $468 million is due through May 2027, the end of the company's fiscal year. Payments rise to $1.58 billion the following year and $2.36 billion the year after. Another $26.6 billion is due after May 2031.

    It has been revealed that the reason is largely construction. As of the 10-Q's filing, Applied Digital had 250 megawatts of AI data center capacity running at its Polaris Forge 1 campus in Ellendale, North Dakota, out of 1,410 megawatts under contract. Its other buildings are scheduled to come online between late 2026 and 2028. A 210-megawatt building leased in June to another investment-grade hyperscaler isn't due until the first half of 2028.

    The company's annual report spells out what happens if building falls behind schedule: "Under certain circumstances, lessees may have the right to terminate applicable leases if there are significant delays in construction." It adds that Applied Digital "may not be able to release the applicable data center in a timely or profitable manner.".

    Recent findings suggest that the organization's debt terms already account for that possibility. Under the terms of the 7% notes due 2031, issued by an Applied Digital subsidiary, if that subsidiary receives certain termination fees from a tenant, it generally must use them to pay off the notes, with exceptions if a replacement tenant is found.

    According to recent reports, the construction boom is happening as the firm loads up with debt. Applied Digital's long-term debt rose to $6.26 billion at Aug. 31 from $4.96 billion three months earlier. Interest expense for the quarter was $77.4 million, up from $8 million a year before. Meanwhile, revenue grew to $341.9 million from $80.9 million, but the company posted an operating loss of $62.4 million. It ended the quarter with $2.95 billion in cash.

    This combination is common for data center stocks in a building phase, but it also means the firm has little room for delays, since late buildings both push back revenue and give tenants a possible way out.

    The new lease adds another investment-grade tenant, and its 18-year term is longer than the roughly 15-year term on the June lease, but the risk lies in execution. Applied Digital has to finish several large buildings on schedule, keep financing them, and hand them over before tenants' patience runs out.

    In a recent development, the tenants' own spending is a second question. In a commentary published Monday, LPL Financial Chief Equity Strategist Jeffrey Buchbinder noted that the six largest U.S. hyperscalers are expected to generate negative free cash flow in 2026 and 2027, based on Bloomberg estimates. He also wrote that political headwinds will likely slow data center construction, "though probably not until 2028," and that rising financing costs could hurt project feasibility. Several of Applied Digital's buildings are due that year.

    Recent findings suggest that for investors weighing AI stocks tied to the build-out, Applied Digital's next quarterly report should show whether its 2027 construction targets are still on track. Until most of that capacity is in operation, the $41 billion figure reflects the rent the organization expects to collect if construction stays on schedule.

    • In just a single day, Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) stock jumped more than 30%.
    • Investors emphatically gave the move their stamp of approval, with the stock skyrocketing on the day, back to around a $4 trillion valuation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By David Jagielski, CPA – Nov 23, 2026 at 6:40PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    What a turnaround. In just a single day, Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) stock jumped more than 30%. The tech company unveiled that it was reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, who had resigned earlier in the month after multiple extramarital affairs came to light. It also comes after the board said it wasn't considering bringing him back.

    Investors emphatically gave the move their stamp of approval, with the stock skyrocketing on the day, back to around a $4 trillion valuation. It is, however, still down more than 30% from its peak. Given the excitement around Nvidia's stock right now, could it be heading back to $200?

    With the huge rally on Monday, Nvidia's stock is back up to around the levels it was at a few weeks ago, when Huang initially resigned. However, even before the scandal came to light, the stock was already falling from its highs; a month ago, the tech stock was trading at around $210.

    The company's board initially stated it would not take Huang back as CEO. However, by Monday, it unanimously voted to reinstate him. A big part of the reason appears to be due to the government's input. U.S. President Donald Trump has spoken positively of Huang and believed it was in the company's best interests to have him back, and claims he convinced the board to take him back, saying, "I made the deal.".

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    While there's one less question mark around Nvidia's business right now, there are still others looming, including what will happen involving Congress. Huang is scheduled to meet with Congress on Dec. 1, facing questions about a relationship with a possible Chinese spy.

    Trump, however, says he gave Nvidia's board assurances about national security: "We gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot." On the surface, it would appear that issues relating to national security may not be significant enough to warrant any further concern from the organization's board.

    Recent findings suggest that given how volatile the stock has been and the excitement around it, I wouldn't be surprised to see Nvidia shares get back up to $200 in the near future. However, the broader market risk of rising interest rates still looms, which could impact the business and its growth prospects in the longer run.

    In a recent development, for now, the market appears to be focused on the short term; however, this can expose the stock to significant volatility. Investors should tread carefully because while Nvidia's hot today, if market sentiment sours next month due to rising interest rates, things could change rapidly.

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 23, 2026 at 7:11PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Bloom Energy ›.

    Artificial intelligence (AI) is likely to be a world-changing technology, but it uses a huge amount of electricity. AI power demand has been so high that it has driven up electricity costs for everyone, hitting the pocketbooks of everyday people even as inflation is running hot. That's resulted in pushback, with data centers playing a prominent role in the recent midterm elections. That could actually be a net positive for companies like Bloom Energy (BE +18.09%) and Caterpillar (CAT +7.17%). Here's why.

    The current administration in Washington has been very supportive of artificial intelligence. With the House and Senate changing hands next year following significant wins in November's election, support for AI could waver. There are already states that have put up roadblocks to further data center construction. One of the biggest problems is electricity, with a push for data centers to supply their own power to avoid straining the grid.

    In a recent development, that, however, could be a huge win for companies like Bloom Energy and Caterpillar. Bloom Energy makes factory-built hydrogen fuel cells that can be easily deployed where they are needed to provide off-grid power. Caterpillar is best known for making the heavy construction equipment used to build data centers, but it also makes generators used to provide off-grid power.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Sources indicate that if data centers have to bring their own power, Bloom Energy and Cat are primed to help. Notably, Bloom Energy entered 2026 with a $6 billion product backlog, up 140% year over year. That backlog has likely grown throughout the year (it only reports its backlog annually) and could get even bigger in the future. The company, which has lost money for years, is likely to turn profitable in 2026.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    In a recent development, caterpillar ended the third quarter with a record $78 billion backlog, up 96% year over year. While not all of that backlog is tied to its power systems, the bigger takeaway is that demand remains very strong across all its products. That said, management noted that bringing up manufacturing capacity in its power division remains a primary goal because demand is so strong.

    It has been revealed that the shifting political winds in Washington could increase the already strong demand that Bloom Energy and Cat are seeing. But investors need to distinguish between the stocks and the businesses here. AI-related stocks, including both of these companies, have been volatile of late. If you own them or are considering buying them, you need to approach them with a long-term mindset. Another option is to add them to your wish list and be ready to pounce if there is a deep AI-driven bear market.

    The Nasdaq Just Had Its Best Day Since April 2025. Anthropic Stock Fell Anyway.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (672 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, for a while this morning, Anthropic (ANT -1.43%) looked like it would soar today after news of Jensen Huang's dramatic return to Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) broke.
    • But by the closing bell, Anthropic was down 1.4%.
    • Just two trading days after its debut, in what was the year's biggest gain for the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +6.51%), Anthropic stock inched lower.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Johnny Rice – Nov 23, 2026 at 7:22PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    In a recent development, for a while this morning, Anthropic (ANT -1.43%) looked like it would soar today after news of Jensen Huang's dramatic return to Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) broke. Shares of the newly public tech giant opened up 5.4%.

    But by the closing bell, Anthropic was down 1.4%. Not a bad day per se, but consider the gains from the rest of the tech market:.

    Just two trading days after its debut, in what was the year's biggest gain for the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +6.51%), Anthropic stock inched lower. Why did the Claude maker's stock miss out on most of the marketwide rally?

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Sources indicate that nvidia's board revealed this morning that it was bringing Huang back as CEO, president, and board member. That's just under a week after Board Chair Harvey Jones told investors that Huang's return was not on the table. The official announcement said that the board had "received input from senior levels of the United States government," giving it confidence that "Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk.".

    In a recent development, the government input was, in fact, from the most senior of senior levels: the U.S. President. Trump told CNBC that he spoke with the board "directly and indirectly" to advocate for Huang's return: "I convinced them." Trump reassured the board that he did not pose a national security threat after Attorney General Todd Blanche assured the President that investigators had no evidence to suggest wrongdoing.

    Whatever the full reasoning behind that led to the board's decision, the move -- a shock to many -- breathed life into an ailing AI trade that was in serious need of good news; the Nasdaq  turned red for 2026 on Friday after entering a correction earlier in the month.

    So why did Anthropic sit this one out?

    A few reasons: first, Reuters reported that President Trump -- Vice President JD Vance, too -- intervened in part because they saw Huang as crucial to keeping American companies competitive in open-weight AI -- a market in which China leads.

    Open-weight models are offered to the public -- often for free -- to download, tweak, adapt, and run however and wherever they see fit.

    That stands in stark contrast to the closed models of Anthropic and rival OpenAI, which offer comparatively little in the way of customization and, most importantly, run in the cloud and can only be accessed through the organization. That ensures they get paid every time you use their models. To state the obvious, they do not get paid if a company opts for an open-weight model. That makes them a potential threat to Anthropic's growth -- a pretty substantial one.

    Nvidia, on the other hand, gets paid no matter what models get used, so long as the servers powering the model use its chips. More open-weight models mean more potential customers. That's why Jensen Huang has been an advocate, making several major investments in open-weight developers.

    Whether or not Huang is at the helm, open-weight models pose a genuine threat to Anthropic's business. It is one of the core reasons I would avoid the stock. At the moment, Anthropic's moat -- the thing keeping customers paying Anthropic and not its competitors -- comes almost entirely from having the best models.

    Jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images.

    That's not a very strong one in my opinion, and over time, I see Anthropic struggling to keep customers from switching workloads over to cheaper open-weight alternatives.
