    If a Stock Market Crash Is Coming, Warren Buffett Says This Is the Best Move Investors Should Make

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (948 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that despite stubborn inflation, rising interest rates, geopolitical conflicts, and considerable economic uncertainty, the S&P 500 (^GSPC +4.73%), Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +6.51%), and Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI +3.01%) have delivered impressive returns over the last four years.
    • Those fears are intensifying as artificial intelligence (AI) stocks retreat from record highs.
    • Fortunately, legendary investor Warren Buffett has a simple strategy for navigating periods of market turbulence.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Spatacco – Nov 23, 2026 at 8:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    Recent findings suggest that despite stubborn inflation, rising interest rates, geopolitical conflicts, and considerable economic uncertainty, the S&P 500 (^GSPC +4.73%), Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +6.51%), and Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI +3.01%) have delivered impressive returns over the last four years. However, this rapid appreciation of stocks has also raised concerns that a bubble could be forming.

    Those fears are intensifying as artificial intelligence (AI) stocks retreat from record highs. Both the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 recently entered correction territory, although both indexes are rebounding sharply as Jensen Huang returns to the CEO position of Nvidia.

    Fortunately, legendary investor Warren Buffett has a simple strategy for navigating periods of market turbulence.

    Between Nov. 30, 2022 -- the day ChatGPT was launched to the public -- and Nov. 20, 2026, the S&P 500 advanced approximately 69%, equivalent to an annualized gain of roughly 14%. The Nasdaq performed even better, climbing roughly 97%, or 18% annually.

    It has been revealed that much of this growth was driven by the AI revolution. Companies designing AI chips, providing cloud infrastructure, and building enterprise software have attracted outsize interest from growth investors. Meanwhile, demand for data centers is creating opportunities throughout the economy. Utilities, energy producers, industrial equipment manufacturers, and construction companies are increasingly benefiting from the infrastructure spending required to support AI adoption.

    Recent findings suggest that however, enthusiasm surrounding AI is also pushing stock market valuations toward historically expensive levels. One revealing indicator is the Shiller cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio, which measures the S&P 500's price relative to its average inflation-adjusted earnings over the last 10 years.

    Unlike a traditional price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, CAPE readings smooth out short-term fluctuations in earnings. This makes it useful for assessing long-term valuations. Historically, the metric has averaged 17.7, meaning investors have generally paid around $18 for every dollar of normalized earnings.

    Shiller CAPE Ratio data by YCharts.

    Right now, the CAPE ratio sits around 41 -- dangerously close to its highest level in history. That places valuations at more than twice their historical average and well above the threshold that has occasionally preceded major market drawdowns.

    Sources indicate that for perspective, the CAPE ratio exceeded 30 before the 1929 stock market crash. During this period, the Dow plunged 89% through 1932. Meanwhile, the CAPE ratio reached an all-time high of 44 during the dot-com era. Once the bubble burst, the Nasdaq collapsed 77% between March 2000 and October 2002 while the S&P 500 declined approximately 49%.

    It has been revealed that these examples underscore why elevated valuations deserve attention. With that stated, the CAPE ratio is not a reliable indicator of what the market will do in the near term. Moreover, readings between 30 and 40 do not automatically mean a crash is imminent. Rather, elevated CAPE ratios have historically been associated with subdued returns in the immediate years following a crash.

    Although bubbles can produce stomach-churning losses in the short term, history demonstrates the resilience of the stock market. The S&P 500 has endured the Great Depression, multiple recessions, wars, financial crises, and numerous presidential administrations while continuing to generate long-term wealth.

    Consider what happened to investors who bought stocks right at the height of the dot-com bubble. The Nasdaq peaked at approximately 5,048 in March 2000 before collapsing nearly 77% over the following two and a half years. Nevertheless, the index eventually recovered and surpassed its previous record in 2015.

    It has been revealed that as of this writing (Nov. 23), the Nasdaq stands near 24,142, representing 386% appreciation from its dot-com era peak. That's respectable even for someone who invested at one of the worst possible moments in modern market history.

    The S&P 500 tells a similar story. Its March 2000 peak was 1,527, compared with roughly 7,224 as of this writing. That represents a gain of 375% despite the dot-com collapse, the 2008 financial crisis, and the COVID-19 crash.

    The lesson here is straightforward: Even investors who bought stocks at historically expensive valuations eventually generated multibagger gains by remaining invested.

    In a recent development, in Berkshire Hathaway's shareholder letter from 2016, Buffett acknowledged that market declines were inevitable. But the "Oracle of Omaha" also emphasized that no one can reliably forecast when they will occur. Buffett observed:.

    Industry observers note that buffett's investment philosophy emphasizes remaining invested in productive businesses rather than repeatedly moving between stocks and cash based on market predictions. Investors who sell during downturns face two difficult decisions: determining when to exit and deciding when to reinvest.

    It has been revealed that getting either decision wrong often has consequences. Stock market recoveries tend to begin when economic conditions still appear bleak, meaning investors who wait for uncertainty to disappear end up missing out on gains.

    For investors with a long-term time horizon, a prudent approach involves maintaining a diversified portfolio, holding an appropriate cash reserve, and continuing to invest through periods of volatility. Cash will provide the financial flexibility to buy the dip in quality companies when market sell-offs create compelling opportunities.

    At the end of the day, building wealth requires staying invested through market volatility rather than trying to avoid every downturn.

Management delivered 30 logical qubits using just 80 physical qubits -- a ratio under three physical qubits per logical qubit -- which shows its neutral-atom hardware, controlled by light lasers, requires less physical equipment to perform complex calculations.

    In a recent development, commercial interest is converting into hard commitments as system sales expand globally. Total remaining performance obligations -- unbilled contract value committed under signed agreements -- reached $51.2 million in the quarter, laying a firm foundation for computing sales to expand in 2027.

    Quantum sensing platforms generate steady cash flow while quantum computing technology matures. A $20 million expansion from NASA to an existing total gravity-sensing contract illustrates how government agencies rely on the company's precise atomic measurements for space and defense missions.

    Sources indicate that demand for neutral-atom architecture is building across commercial and defense markets, backed by $560 million in cash and short-term investments. Management is prioritizing manufacturing expansion and system delivery timelines as customer engagement accelerates.

    Scaling hardware shipments remains essential for generating operating leverage as computing revenue expands alongside established sensing operations.

    • Is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).

    Is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

    Sources indicate that first, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout quickly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

    The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

    According to recent reports, zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three vital forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:.

    This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

    For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

    The following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

    Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

    The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

    The major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

    That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

    One notable clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

    According to recent reports, any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

    We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

    The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

    Recent findings suggest that from here, it's all about the follow through. We don't need to see latest highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (640 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    CFO Colette Kress Just Made This Subtle Shift That Could Save Nvidia Shareholders

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (640 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) continues to impress shareholders.
    • Unfortunately for shareholders, CEO Jensen Huang financed much of this growth through "circular financing," in which the manufacturer finances customers to sell products.
    • Industry observers note that CFO Colette Kress, who was briefly interim CEO, questioned this strategy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Will Healy – Nov 23, 2026 at 8:06PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) continues to impress shareholders. Even though large companies tend to grow slowly, Nvidia has challenged that assertion by delivering triple-digit revenue growth, much as it did in the third quarter of fiscal 2027 (ended Oct. 25).

    Unfortunately for shareholders, CEO Jensen Huang financed much of this growth through "circular financing," in which the manufacturer finances customers to sell products.

    Industry observers note that CFO Colette Kress, who was briefly interim CEO, questioned this strategy. She reined in much of this financial support for other companies' artificial intelligence (AI) projects. Assuming Huang follows her lead, here's how this approach could save Nvidia shareholders.

    In recent months, investors have become more concerned about how Nvidia generated its revenue growth.

    Nvidia was to provide financial backing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio. Huang wanted to backstop $250 billion of OpenAI purchases, but Kress stepped in to cut that commitment to $105 billion.

    Although Kress has rejected the "circular financing" label, as interim CEO, she stated on the third-quarter 2027 earnings call that Nvidia would be "disciplined and selective" in its support for the neoclouds, which will likely reassure those investors who questioned Huang's prior approach.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    This is critical for investors because analysts often view such financing as consistent with the end stage of a boom.

    According to recent reports, they have good reason to worry. Cisco Systems (CSCO +6.80%) was at the center of the dot-com boom when it backstopped several of its customers. In 2001, Cisco famously had to write down $2.25 billion in one quarter when several of the customers it backed declared bankruptcy. That write-down contributed to a stock price decline so profound that it took 26 years for its stock to return to its 2000 high.

    According to recent reports, with "everything Kress told us," the firm carries around $118 billion in guarantees, several orders of magnitude higher than Cisco's write-down. Still, if projects fall behind schedule, the company will now revoke guarantees, a move that could shield it from painful write-offs later.

    Moreover, Nvidia may not be vulnerable to a slump as severe as Cisco's. Nvidia's 18 P/E ratio as of Nov. 23 is a tiny fraction of the 222 P/E ratio that Cisco reached in early 2000, suggesting less downside if an AI bust occurs.

    In a recent development, furthermore, Kress's approach did not appear to meaningfully slow Nvidia, even in the short term. For fiscal Q4, it guided for $130 billion in revenue at the midpoint, a 91% year-over-year increase if that forecast holds. While that is slightly less than fiscal Q3's 103% revenue increase, it may be a small price to pay to mitigate the specter of massive write-downs later.

    Kress's move to rein in customer financing could alleviate a significant worry about the stock, assuming Huang follows his advice now that he has returned as CEO.

    Indeed, the possibility of bankruptcies among major customers leaves Nvidia financially exposed, and that vulnerability could hurt the stock.

    In a recent development, nonetheless, Kress's decision to be "disciplined and selective" about customer financing addresses a key concern with Nvidia's current business approach. While it may mean somewhat slower growth, the prospect of reduced financial exposure should an AI bust occur is likely a wise move in the long run.

    • Sources indicate that blackRock offers exposure to one of the most diversified businesses in asset management.
    • Industry observers note that on top of that, the firm sees broad demand, attracting massive inflows across equities, fixed-income investments, alternative investments, and cash.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Rick Orford – Nov 23, 2026 at 8:38PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Blackstone ›.

    Industry observers note that blackRock (BLK +3.88%) and Blackstone (BX +4.57%) each oversee more than $1 trillion in assets, making them two of the largest asset management firms worldwide. But with one trading closer to its 52-week high and the other down sharply this year, the question is: Which stock offers the more attractive opportunity for buyers?

    Sources indicate that blackRock offers exposure to one of the most diversified businesses in asset management. With $15.5 trillion in assets under management (AUM) at the end of the third quarter, up 15% from the previous year, the manufacturer has built an enormous platform spanning index funds, exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and private markets.

    Industry observers note that on top of that, the firm sees broad demand, attracting massive inflows across equities, fixed-income investments, alternative investments, and cash. For example, its iShares ETF business remains an key growth engine, while its active investment strategies attract capital from investors seeking opportunities beyond passive index investing.

    Its third-quarter performance further strengthened the bull case in favor of the stock. Its third-quarter revenue rose 19% year over year, while adjusted earnings per share (EPS) climbed 38%. Looking ahead, its ability to attract fresh money while expanding its technology and private markets businesses gives it several avenues for continued earnings growth.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    The main drawback is valuation. So far this year, BlackRock stock is up about 5% and trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio based on estimated earnings performance of about 18, which means investors are paying about $18 for every $1 of expected earnings. That leaves less room for error if market conditions deteriorate or inflows slow down.

    Another organization has also built its business around alternative assets, giving investors exposure to private equity, real estate, and infrastructure.

    Blackstone has also established itself as one of the biggest names in alternative-asset management, with $1.4 trillion in AUM as of the third quarter. More broadly, its latest results suggest that investor demand remains healthy despite a challenging backdrop for private markets. Specifically, the manufacturer attracted $63.3 billion in latest money, bringing its trailing 12-month (TTM) inflows to $271.6 billion.

    It has been revealed that beyond inflows, one encouraging development is the growth of its perpetual capital business, which reached $562 billion. These investment vehicles are designed to provide capital without the fixed fund life and fundraising cycles associated with traditional private equity funds. This gives Blackstone a larger pool of relatively stable capital that can support more predictable fee revenue over time.

    Blackstone is also benefiting from several major investment themes, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), energy infrastructure, and private credit. After all, building data centers, expanding electricity capacity, and financing AI infrastructure requires enormous amounts of capital. And Blackstone has established investment platforms across all these themes, allowing it to participate in the biggest opportunities of the next decade.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Blackstone shares have fallen almost 27% this year, but that has made its valuation more reasonable, with the stock trading at a forward P/E of about 16. Looking ahead, if transaction activity improves and fundraising accelerates, the stock could recover well.

    Overall, both BlackRock and Blackstone offer exposure to the growing asset management industry, but their valuations and growth drivers present different opportunities for investors.

    Sources indicate that blackRock offers scale, diversification, and strong earnings growth, making it appealing to investors seeking steady long-term growth, although its premium valuation limits the margin for error. Blackstone offers exposure to private markets and AI infrastructure at a considerably lower price, potentially giving investors greater upside if the company recovers. In other words, these giants appeal to different buyers: BlackRock is steadier, Blackstone is riskier. But each looks like a buy.

    #96976. A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (631 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (631 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct.
    • However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive.
    • Recent findings suggest that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct. 6. The market despises uncertainty, and losing a visionary founder, particularly one without a well-telegraphed succession plan, makes it worse.

    However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive. Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a significant haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact. While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the tech giant's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him. The company's structural advantage in the global artificial intelligence rollout persists.

    Recent findings suggest that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options. Huang's departure guarantees that Nvidia will be operating under a cloud of transition for the foreseeable future. Executing a permanent CEO search while navigating global regulatory scrutiny takes time. Consequently, Nvidia's implied volatility (IV)—the market's pricing of expected future price swings — has spiked to highs not seen since the tariff tantrum in the first half of 2025, and this elevated IV is highly likely to persist for several months as the leadership drama slowly unfolds.

    According to recent reports, this prolonged period of high implied volatility can be a goldmine for option sellers, specifically those executing options overlays such as covered call strategies. When you buy NVDA shares at these depressed levels and simultaneously sell out-of-the-money call options against your position, the premiums you collect are directly tied to IV. Because fear and transition-related uncertainty have dramatically inflated these option prices, the income generated from selling covered calls is now significantly higher than usual.

    Sources indicate that this lowers the risk profile of holding the stock considerably over time. Consistently collecting these inflated premiums systematically lowers your overall cost basis in the underlying shares. If the stock trades sideways or recovers slowly during the CEO search, you are generating an outsized cash yield on a stagnant asset. If the stock experiences further downside turbulence, the heavy premium income acts as a substantial downside buffer, meaningfully reducing the strategy's overall risk over time.

    By deploying a persistent covered call strategy, investors can leverage the exact fear driving the stock down to generate robust, risk-reducing income while maintaining exposure to the undeniable future of AI.

    By Marc Guberti – Nov 23, 2026 at 9:31PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Tesla ›.

    It has been revealed that humanoid robots grab people's attention as they walk on sidewalks. Granted, it's a rare sight since this technology is in its early stages, but there is plenty of excitement about the future.

    While many start-ups are creating their own humanoid robots, it may be better for investors to invest in the companies selling shovels during a gold rush. Once hints of humanoid robotics leaders become more apparent and finances improve, it may be worth considering smaller companies.

    For now, these three tech giants look well-positioned for the humanoid robot boom.

    Image source: Agility Robotics.

    Tesla (TSLA +11.46%) is the most direct, established American firm for exposure to humanoid robots. The company has been developing its Optimus robot segment for several years and has sufficient revenue and profits to ensure financial sustainability.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Revenue reached $28 billion in Q3, which was roughly flat year over year. The firm's "Services and other revenue" component was the only part of the business to grow, suggesting that Tesla's future growth will have to come from robots.

    Industry observers note that net income wasn't as exciting, down 43% year over year, but $787 million in pure profit is still more impressive than humanoid robot start-up companies. While Tesla has been a volatile growth stock, it's actually one of the least-risky ways to gain exposure to humanoid robots. Tesla anticipates delivering orders in late 2027.

    Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) isn't specifically a robotics stock, but its artificial intelligence chips are foundational for robotics. As demand for humanoid robots soars, Nvidia chips will gain even more traction. Grand View Research projects a 38.2% CAGR for the humanoid robot market through 2033, indicating the type of momentum Nvidia can ride.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    While high demand for humanoid robots is critical to Tesla's long-term investment thesis, Nvidia continues to perform well in current times. Revenue surged 103% year over year in the firm's fiscal 2027 third quarter, and its impressive guidance shows it is taking steps to gain market share.

    Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress highlighted that the company's roadmap is on track and that demand is still booming. That's the type of news investors want to hear as 2026 comes to a close, and it further silences concerns about an AI bubble.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile, AI stocks have been trending downward for several weeks. Fundamentals are still growing, but the best explanation may be concerns about higher rates and uncertainty with oil, even as the commodity's price continues to trend downward.

    In any event, this sharp correction has produced an enticing valuation for Nvidia, making it cheaper than most S&P 500 (^GSPC +4.73%) stocks and putting it deep into value-stock territory.

    Micron (MU +19.04%) plays a similar role to Nvidia in humanoid robots. They require vast amounts of memory to interact with the world and learn from their training, and Micron's chips fill in the gap.

    Its technology will be part of the humanoid robot bedrock, and, like Nvidia, Micron isn't waiting for these robots to become mainstream before delivering compelling financial results.

    Sources indicate that micron anticipates $61.5 billion in fiscal 2027 first-quarter revenue. That's more than a 4x increase from the $13.64 billion Micron generated in the same quarter last year. Micron has established a good reputation for beating the high end of its guidance throughout the AI boom, which makes a 5x growth rate possible.

    Recent findings suggest that multi-year customer deals highlight the sustainability of the AI boom, but even with these bullish catalysts, Micron has been caught in the recent negative sentiment of the AI trade. It has a P/E ratio below 10, which offers an attractive entry point for investors who can wait out the current volatility.

    It's Thanksgiving week in the NBA and looking back, fantasy basketball managers have plenty to be thankful for (if they were able to avoid the injury bug after the first month-plus of the 2026-27 season).

    In Yahoo High Score fantasy basketball, it was a pretty eventful Week 5 with a few 50-burgers and three players landing in the perfect lineup thanks to an overtime track meet between the Bulls and Nuggets on Sunday. Let's dive into the perfect lineup and break down the top performers.

    Week 5 High Score perfect lineup.

    Industry observers note that josh Giddey: The Bulls guard had been off to a slow start to the season, averaging just 8.5 points and 7.5 assists per game in six contests in the opening month. But since November came along, Giddey has upped his game a bit, though managers would like to see him be more aggressive on offense. But that unselfishness is why Giddey landed in the perfect lineup, posting 23 points, 14 rebounds and 22 assists for 84 fantasy points in the Bulls' OT loss to Denver on Sunday. Chicago has three gettable matchups in Week 6, so be sure to get Giddey in those lineups.

    Jamal Murray: The Nuggets' guard is pacing toward his best NBA season, averaging 26.2 points per game after Sunday's 45-point outburst in the win over Chicago. That point-per-minute performance awarded Murray 79 fantasy points and one of the guard spots in the perfect lineup. Murray also chipped in 5 rebounds, 7 assists and 5 stocks — pretty good category coverage. A consensus second-round pick preseason, Murray is looking like an early league-winner if he can keep this up.

    Victor Wembanyama: Wow, we didn't expect Wemby to land in this article again (wink). But really, Wembanyama is putting together an MVP campaign so far in 2026-27, and has been arguably the best asset for High Score fantasy basketball (Luka Dončić is really the only one ahead of him right now). After last week's 50-point outing against the Pelicans, Wembanyama now has the two highest single outputs of the season for High Score (110, 97). He'll get another shot to try and top the High Score leaderboard in Week 6 with four games on tap.

    Sources indicate that nikola Jokić: The Joker benefitted from that overtime contest on Sunday, same as Giddey and Murray. It was the Nuggets substantial's second-highest fantasy score of the season with a 37-18-11 triple-double, just his fourth triple-double of the season. Yes, we can say "just" there because we're used to Jokić doing that pretty much every night. While this feels like a slow start by Jokić's standards, he's still the No. 3 asset in fantasy as we're just past the first month of the season.

    Industry observers note that bam Adebayo: The Heat and Adebayo started off the Giannis era with four straight losses but have since gone 10-2 since Oct. 28. Adebayo is starting to find his groove on offense, averaging north of 20 points per game in November with 8.4 rebounds, 3.9 assits and nearly 3.0 stocks per contest. Other than a game in which he left early due to injury, Adebayo has at least 40 fantasy points in six straight games. Miami has a rough sledding up in Week 6 with road games against Eastern Conference rivals — the Sixers, Knicks and Cavaliers.

    Sources indicate that tyler Herro: The former Heat guard who was the centerpiece of the Giannis deal this offseason, Herro was expected to join Milwaukee and lead the team in scoring. That's been the case, though it hasn't led to much winning for the Bucks. That doesn't matter to us in fantasy, just as long as Herro is filling up the score sheet. Last Saturday, Herro scored a career-high 50 points with 11 boards and 7 assists in a close loss to Philadelphia. Milwaukee has a four-game week with some spots where Herro can showcase that scoring touch again.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (861 w)

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Anthropic Stock Fell About 20% From Its First Trade in Its First 2 Days. Here's the Price at Which I'd Buy It.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (861 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Shares of Claude maker Anthropic (ANT -1.43%) had a rough welcome to the public market.
    • 20, shares had sunk to $88.91 -- around 20% under the first trade.
    • Even after the drop, Anthropic's valuation is about $1.19 trillion.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 23, 2026 at 9:47PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    Shares of Claude maker Anthropic (ANT -1.43%) had a rough welcome to the public market. The stock's first trade on Thursday, Nov. 19, came at $111.50. It was around 34% over the $83 a share the manufacturer set for its initial public offering (IPO) a day earlier.

    By the close on Friday, Nov. 20, shares had sunk to $88.91 -- around 20% under the first trade. They even dipped to $83.05 in Friday's session, just 5 cents over the IPO price, on a day the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +6.51%) lost around 5%.

    Even after the drop, Anthropic's valuation is about $1.19 trillion. That means investors are paying around 34 times sales, based on the $35 billion or so in revenue the company took in over the 12 months through September.

    Recent findings suggest that at what price would the stock be worth buying? I'd put it at $75 a share, around 16% below Friday's close and about 10% under the IPO price. Here's how I get there.

    Showing how fast its Claude artificial intelligence (AI) models have caught on with firms, Anthropic's third-quarter revenue climbed 1,127% year over year to around $17.0 billion. The tech giant's revenue for 2025 was around $4.6 billion. However, its sequential growth slowed sharply in the last quarter. Anthropic's revenue climbed around 132% from the previous quarter in the first quarter of 2026 and about 144% in the second quarter, but only about 47% in the third.

    Recent findings suggest that sure, 47% growth in one quarter is still impressive for a organization this size. But it's well below the 144% a quarter earlier, and I think the slower pace is the better guide to the year ahead.

    Anthropic's third-quarter operating loss was $567 million, versus operating income of $974 million in the second quarter.

    In a recent development, the firm remarked the swing was largely due to $5.0 billion of compute bought under short-term commitments, which now costs much more than compute under its multi-year deals. Anthropic also took $2.0 billion of non-cash charges linked to its donation matching program.

    Sources indicate that compute is Anthropic's largest operating cost. Its compute and infrastructure expenses fell to 48% of revenue in the second quarter, down from 72% in the first, before rising back to 58% in the third. In other words, the improvement that took the tech giant to an operating profit in Q2 partly reversed a quarter later.

    Also, as of and after Sept. 30, Anthropic had committed to around $900.9 billion in spending, almost all of it on compute and infrastructure. Around $70.7 billion of that is due over the following 12 months.

    True, Anthropic can afford a lot. Including the offering, it had around $245 billion in cash and short-term investments on a pro forma basis. But a dollar of Anthropic's revenue arguably isn't worth as much as a dollar of revenue at a software-as-a-service business when more than half of it goes straight back out to pay for compute.

    In a recent development, say Anthropic's revenue rises around 16% each quarter on average in the next year, about a third of its third-quarter rate. Revenue for the next four quarters would then total about $100 billion.

    That sounds like a fair assumption to me, but it isn't a given. Anthropic said in its prospectus that it expects its revenue growth rate to fall over time. And its customer usage has tended to slip around the holidays.

    Given how much of every revenue dollar goes to compute, I'd want to pay no more than about 10 times that forward revenue. At Friday's close, investors were paying about 17.5 times sales based on Anthropic's annualized third-quarter revenue. At 10 times sales, Anthropic's market cap might be around $1 trillion.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    In a recent development, split $1 trillion across the 13.4 billion or so shares outstanding after the offering, and you get around $75 a share. And I wouldn't go above that, because the share count might rise when employee stock awards vest and convertible notes convert.

    There's also more stock headed to the market. Up to 315 million shares owned by Anthropic's non-founder directors, officers, employees, and consultants became eligible for sale on the first trading day.

    According to recent reports, anthropic is arguably one of the most impressive companies to go public in years. But at Friday's close of around $89 a share, buyers were paying for fast growth to last and for compute costs to drop back down.

    At $75 or below, I'd buy shares -- maybe in stages. Above that, I'm happy to wait.

    Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1105 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.
    • Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.
    • The much more widely held B shares closed at upcoming highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.

    Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.

    The much more widely held B shares closed at upcoming highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.

    The gains are in sharp contrast to the S&P 500's 1.2% dip as investors appear to be seeing Berkshire as a relatively safe haven amid worries about AI stocks and spending.

    Both Berkshire classes were up 3.9% on the week as the S&P advanced by 2.5%, its best week since early August.

    Berkshire's B shares are now 7.5 percentage points ahead of the benchmark for the year so far.

    After erasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement losses three weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.

    They've gained around 29% since last August's lows and are up around 18% year-to-date.

    Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.

    We won't know for sure until then, but numbers in the firm's third quarter 10-Q, released last Saturday, indicate Berkshire continued to reduce its Bank of America stake.

    It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.

    As of June 30, Berkshire reported holding 483.4 million BAC shares valued now at $24.7 billion, it's fifth largest equity position.

    On June 30, 2024, before the selling began, Berkshire owned just over 1 billion shares valued at $41.1 billion.

    Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.

    If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.

    The belief Berkshire sold more BAC shares in the third quarter is based on a $372 million reduction in the cost basis for equities categorized by the company as "banks, insurance, and finance.".

    The 10-Q also reports $2.2 billion of pretax gains from equity sales.

    Barron's notes Bank of America and American Express are the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks latest CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to come in his February letter to shareholders.

    In any case, Berkshire's almost 23% stake in Amex would have required it to rapidly disclose any sales.

    Based on the numbers in the 10-Q, the warrants Berkshire received as part of a 2011 $5 billion investment in the bank that it used in 2017 to buy 700 million shares at $7.14 each, and BAC's average stock price in the quarter, Barron's estimates 30 to 40 million shares may have been sold.

    That would be roughly in line with the 30.2 million shares sold in the second quarter.

    The case isn't as good, but Barron's thinks Berkshire may have bought more Alphabet shares in the period. That's based on a $2.3 billion increase in the cost basis for the category that includes Google's parent.

    Overall, it looks like it will be a relatively quiet quarter with $2.4 billion in equity purchases and $2.8 billion in sales.

    In the first quarter, Berkshire bought $15.9 billion and sold $24.1 billion of equities. In the second quarter, it purchased $23.5 billion and sold $3.7 billion.

    All those numbers exclude the tech giant's buybacks of its own stock.

    In a term sheet filed early Friday, Berkshire Hathaway indicates it is selling more than 182 billion yen ($1.1 billion) worth of bonds with maturities between 2029 and 2056 and annual interest rates between 2.6% and 4.6%.

    Bloomberg points out the rates, compared to benchmarks, are higher than its previous sale this year.

    It quotes a fund manager as saying market sentiment "has become more sensitive," forcing issuers to make their offerings more attractive.

    In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.

    Berkshire uses the proceeds from the yen-denominated bonds to protect its ongoing investments in Japanese stocks from currency fluctuations.

    Some links may require a subscription:.

    Warren Buffett recommends Benjamin Graham's book, "The Intelligent Investor," and outlines what he considers Graham's three most key ideas.

    You know, I obviously recommend, first and foremost, [Benjamin Graham's] "The Intelligent Investor," with chapters eight and 20 are the ones that you really should read.

    Two of the — well, all of the key ideas in investing, really, are in that book, because there's only about three ideas. And those — two of them are emphasized in those two chapters...

    One is that — to think of yourself — to think of investing as owning a business and not buying something that wiggles around in price.

    Industry observers note that and the second one is your attitude, which ties in with that, the attitude toward the market, that's covered in chapter eight. And if you have the proper attitude toward market movements, it's an enormous help in securities.

    And the final chapter is on the margin of safety, which means, don't try and drive a 9,800-pound truck over a bridge that says it's, you know, "Capacity: 10,000 pounds." But go down the road a little bit and find one that says, "Capacity: 15,000 pounds.".

    SpaceX Stock Is Down 39% From Its High. Here's What Has to Happen Before I'd Buy.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (645 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.
    • Sources indicate that it's a bit of a riddle: A stock loses nearly 40% of its value, yet still looks expensive by traditional metrics.
    • SpaceX shares have dropped to $136, a roughly 39% decline from an all-time high of about $225.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Steven Porrello – Nov 23, 2026 at 10:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.

    Sources indicate that it's a bit of a riddle: A stock loses nearly 40% of its value, yet still looks expensive by traditional metrics. If that rings a bell, you're likely thinking of the predicament facing investors interested in Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +4.35%), better known as SpaceX.

    SpaceX shares have dropped to $136, a roughly 39% decline from an all-time high of about $225. Even after that considerable decline, SpaceX still carries a sizable valuation -- about $1.9 trillion at this writing.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    What would it take for me to buy SpaceX stock? Has its recent decline brought it any closer to that point?

    Recent findings suggest that spaceX is a behemoth of a business. Three-headed, fast-growing, and formidable, it operates across three segments: rockets and spacecraft (Space), a global communications network (Starlink), and artificial intelligence (Super Intelligence).

    Most people would recognize the first category. Rockets and spacecraft are, in fact, SpaceX's bread and butter, but they're not the business's breadwinner -- at least, not by revenue. That distinction belongs to its AI division, which it calls Super Intelligence. The business generated an impressive $7.6 billion in revenue in the third quarter alone. Connectivity comes second, with $5.2 billion, while rockets and spacecraft contributed about $1.8 billion.

    Revenue growth is rarely a thumbs-down, but it's even sweeter when the manufacturer keeps more of those extra dollars. Here, too, SpaceX gets a gold star: It reported $4.4 billion in net income for Q3, up substantially from a $1.1 billion loss the previous year. That's a great turnaround for a company investing so heavily in its future -- so why am I not investing in SpaceX today?

    Previously, my concern about SpaceX stock was its valuation. That is still my concern; the stock trades at roughly 60 times trailing sales, more than 16 times the S&P 500 (^GSPC +4.73%). Now there's another thing holding me back -- the cost of its growth.

    According to recent reports, during the first nine months of 2026, SpaceX generated about $13 billion in operating cash flow but spent a staggering $48 billion on capital expenditures, roughly $40 billion of which was on its AI business. That works out to about $35 billion in negative free cash flow for the year -- so far. Management is expecting to spend another $35 billion to $40 billion in the fourth quarter alone.

    It has been revealed that obviously, it isn't a bad thing to spend aggressively to grow a business -- and SpaceX has three of them. What worries me is the risks that come with spending billions on AI infrastructure, where the tech giant faces some pretty deep-pocketed competitors. They include Microsoft (MSFT +1.65%), Amazon (AMZN +3.47%), and Alphabet (GOOGL +6.34%) (GOOG +5.88%), just to name the substantial ones. True, SpaceX has shown that it can compete in this market, but whether it can create the same strong competitive advantages that have made it dominant in rockets and satellite communications remains to be seen.

    With tens of billions being thrown at AI, I want some proof that the investment will pay off. Indeed, at a lower valuation, I might be willing to take that risk, but at 60 times trailing sales -- no thanks. I'm fine letting this one play out for now.

    Industry News: Nvidia Just Built Agent Security Into Its Chips. What Does That Mean for CrowdStrike?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • With all the buzz surrounding Nvidia's (NVDA +31.48%) earnings report on Nov.
    • In the organization's earnings call with analysts, CFO Colette Kress discussed Nvidia's intends to secure artificial intelligence (AI) agents, and one of the companies she mentioned was cybersecurity specialist CrowdStrike (CRWD -8.92%).
    • That's a name familiar to Nvidia investors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Patrick Sanders – Nov 23, 2026 at 10:17PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than CrowdStrike ›.

    With all the buzz surrounding Nvidia's (NVDA +31.48%) earnings report on Nov. 17 and the turmoil brought on by Jensen Huang's resignation and reinstatement, you may have overlooked something interesting unrelated to financial results.

    In the organization's earnings call with analysts, CFO Colette Kress discussed Nvidia's intends to secure artificial intelligence (AI) agents, and one of the companies she mentioned was cybersecurity specialist CrowdStrike (CRWD -8.92%).

    That's a name familiar to Nvidia investors. In September, Huang called CrowdStrike Nvidia’s top cybersecurity partner. The companies were already collaborating on AI-powered security software.

    It has been revealed that now that relationship is getting bigger. Nvidia is putting security controls directly into the computing infrastructure that runs AI agents. And CrowdStrike is helping to provide the protection.

    Sources indicate that AI agents are often much more powerful than the chatbots most people are familiar with, and they're getting more powerful every day. Thanks to agentic AI, agents can perform tasks, access databases, execute software, and interact with other systems.

    That's useful if you want your agent to help you create a shopping list, schedule a doctor's appointment, or order a prescription refill.

    Sources indicate that but there are also obvious security concerns right now, as the U.S. has been hit with a variety of computer-related outages affecting banks, the airline industry, and government services. AI agents can be subverted to do harmful things, such as access confidential records or sensitive company data.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia wants to prevent that behavior before it causes damage. In October, the company introduced its OpenShell Reference Architecture, which combines software controls with security enforcement running on Nvidia's BlueField-4 data processing units.

    It has been revealed that openShell limits which files and tools an agent can access. Nvidia Sentry, running on BlueField-4, independently monitors agent behavior and enforces security policies at the hardware level. Nvidia notes that Sentry can quarantine and stop an agent that attempts to operate outside its permitted boundaries in milliseconds.

    In a recent development, kress emphasized the technology during the recent earnings call and identified CrowdStrike among the companies working with Nvidia on OpenShell. It's part of a relationship between Nvidia and CrowdStrike that is developing rapidly.

    In September, CrowdStrike introduced SafeMind, an AI cybersecurity system built using Nvidia's Nemotron models. By using offensive and defensive AI models to identify vulnerabilities and improve protection, SafeMind achieved a 29% higher detection rate and six times faster remediation than the comparison models in its evaluations, CrowdStrike stated.

    Then in October, CrowdStrike announced it was integrating Falcon Guardian, its AI detection and response product, with Nvidia OpenShell. It also announced plans to integrate with Nvidia Sentry on BlueField-4.

    Nvidia's hardware provides another layer of enforcement -- CrowdStrike can supply the intelligence needed to recognize threats, while Nvidia's infrastructure can help enforce restrictions.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    According to recent reports, businesses need cybersecurity protection for their employees, devices, cloud applications, and networks. And as they develop and deploy autonomous agents, those agents create additional activity that security teams need to monitor.

    For example, an employee might interact with a handful of applications during the workday. An autonomous agent could execute hundreds of tasks, access multiple databases, and communicate with other agents without requiring constant human involvement.

    That's a more efficient way to work, but it also creates a potentially enormous amount of activity for security companies to monitor to make sure someone isn't misusing an AI agent, or that the AI agent hasn't gone rogue.

    Sources indicate that crowdStrike isn't simply using Nvidia's technology to improve its existing products anymore. It's working to become part of how Nvidia-powered AI agents are secured in the first place -- and, in doing so, to cement the company's position as one of Nvidia's leading security partners.

    NASA Is Handing Out Moon Contracts Again. Intuitive Machines, Firefly, and Redwire All Got Paid. Only 1 Has the Balance Sheet to Keep Winning.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (881 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • NASA is investing more in its lunar exploration program, and three publicly traded space companies in particular are positioned to benefit: Intuitive Machines (LUNR +11.11%), Firefly Aerospace (FLY +8.20%), and Redwire(RDW +13.63%).
    • 7, NASA announced a new round of awards supporting its planned moon base, including lunar transportation, communications, and power infrastructure.
    • In a recent development, NASA recently selected eight companies, including Firefly and Intuitive Machines, to compete for contracts under its next commercial lunar payload services program, known as CLPS 2.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jeff Siegel – Nov 23, 2026 at 10:27PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Firefly Aerospace ›.

    NASA is investing more in its lunar exploration program, and three publicly traded space companies in particular are positioned to benefit: Intuitive Machines (LUNR +11.11%), Firefly Aerospace (FLY +8.20%), and Redwire(RDW +13.63%).

    Sources indicate that on Nov. 7, NASA announced a new round of awards supporting its planned moon base, including lunar transportation, communications, and power infrastructure. All three companies have secured positions in NASA's expanding lunar program, but their financial situations are quite different. Let's take a closer look.

    In a recent development, NASA recently selected eight companies, including Firefly and Intuitive Machines, to compete for contracts under its next commercial lunar payload services program, known as CLPS 2. The program has a maximum value of $10 billion over 10 years. NASA also increased the ceiling of its existing CLPS program from $2.6 billion to $4.2 billion.

    Sources indicate that redwire was selected to provide power-generation technology for NASA's planned mini-communications and solar tower, which will support operations on the lunar surface. The value of that award wasn't disclosed.

    Recent findings suggest that these announcements follow approximately $590 million in lunar delivery contracts unveiled in June, including $144.2 million for Firefly and $148.3 million for Intuitive Machines. Of course, the $10 billion CLPS 2 figure represents a spending ceiling, not guaranteed revenue for participating companies. Individual contracts will still need to be awarded.

    Recent findings suggest that intuitive Machines has been growing promptly. In Q3 2026, revenue reached $269.3 million, up from $52.4 million a year earlier. The organization also generated $66.2 million in operating cash flow and approximately $33.5 million in free cash flow. It also finished September with $463.8 million in cash.

    According to recent reports, those are encouraging numbers, especially for a firm operating in an industry where developing spacecraft and launching missions can swiftly burn through hundreds of millions of dollars. However, Intuitive Machines carries $336.9 million in long-term debt. That's a substantial obligation for a business still expanding its operations and investing in upcoming technology.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Redwire manufactures spacecraft components, solar arrays, and other technologies used in space infrastructure.

    In a recent development, in Q3 2026, revenue reached $109 million, an increase of 5.4% from the previous year. Contracted backlog climbed to a record $619.7 million, and the organization also reported $488.9 million in cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash against approximately $47 million in debt. That's a considerable improvement in its financial position.

    But Redwire remains unprofitable. It reported a $23.2 million net loss in Q3 and an adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) loss of $5.3 million. Indeed, its growing backlog is encouraging, but converting those contracts into profitable operations remains a challenge.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    It has been revealed that firefly's latest financial results make a compelling case for why it could be the strongest of these three companies. At the end of September, Firefly held $534.7 million in cash and short-term investments, compared with just $25.1 million in financial debt. That works out to approximately $510 million in net cash.

    Firefly is also growing quickly. Third-quarter revenue jumped 259% year over year to $110.7 million, while backlog reached a record $1.7 billion. And unlike many companies competing for NASA contracts, Firefly has already demonstrated its ability to land a spacecraft on the Moon.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    In March 2025, its Blue Ghost lander completed the first fully successful commercial lunar landing. Firefly is now preparing additional lunar missions while expanding its launch and national security operations. That gives it an established track record, a substantial backlog, and considerable financial resources to pursue additional contracts.

    To be sure, Firefly does have a history of operating losses and negative operating cash flow. Its cash and short-term investments also declined from approximately $893 million at the end of 2025 to $535 million in September 2026.

    Developing launch vehicles and spacecraft isn't cheap, and future missions will require substantial investment. And there's also no guarantee Firefly will secure a meaningful portion of NASA's new $10 billion program. Still, Firefly has the largest net cash position among these three companies, a $1.7 billion backlog, and a successful lunar landing already under its belt.

    Recent findings suggest that intuitive Machines and Redwire have legitimate opportunities to benefit from NASA's expanding lunar ambitions. But based on their latest financial results, Firefly looks best positioned to compete for additional contracts without taking on substantial latest debt.

    That doesn't automatically make it the best stock to buy. Valuation and execution still count. But if I were choosing one of these three companies based on financial strength and its ability to pursue future lunar contracts, Firefly would be my pick.

    #96944. Average 401(k), IRA balances fall as more workers tap their accounts, Fidelity indicates

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (969 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Average 401(k), IRA balances fall as more workers tap their accounts, Fidelity indicates

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (969 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Retirement account balances fell slightly in the third quarter amid market volatility, according to data released Monday from Fidelity Investments, the nation's largest provider of 401(k) savings plans.
    • Some workers also tapped their retirement accounts for cash, signaling that persistent affordability pressures continue to strain household finances, said Mike Shamrell, Fidelity's vice president of thought leadership.
    • The average 401(k) balance slipped 2% from the previous quarter to $152,500, while the average individual retirement account balance was down 1% to $142,261, Fidelity found.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Retirement account balances fell slightly in the third quarter amid market volatility, according to data released Monday from Fidelity Investments, the nation's largest provider of 401(k) savings plans.

    Some workers also tapped their retirement accounts for cash, signaling that persistent affordability pressures continue to strain household finances, said Mike Shamrell, Fidelity's vice president of thought leadership.

    The average 401(k) balance slipped 2% from the previous quarter to $152,500, while the average individual retirement account balance was down 1% to $142,261, Fidelity found. Both figures hit record highs during the second quarter.

    Despite the third-quarter decline, average balances in IRAs, 401(k)s and 403(b) plans — which are 401(k)-type plans offered by entities such as public schools, churches and nonprofits — are higher year over year and continue to trend up over the long run.

    Sources indicate that wall Street's major averages finished the third quarter on mixed footing, driven in part by the war with Iran, which blocked passage through the Strait of Hormuz, a key transit artery for global energy supplies, and caused oil prices to spike. The stock market's slowdown in the third quarter marked a cooling after the double-digit gains posted in the previous quarter.

    The S&P 500 index added 2.03% over the three-month period, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.9% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ended the quarter 2.2% higher.

    At the same time, financial pressures pushed more savers to reduce their contributions to retirement aims.

    Industry observers note that the average 401(k) contribution rate, including employee and employer contributions, edged down to 14.3% from 14.4% in the second quarter, Fidelity found. Fidelity's recommended combined annual savings benchmark is 15%.

    "We know that there is a lot of concern out there ... [and] people are likely making changes to their personal financial world," Shamrell stated.

    Some savers also dipped into their accounts to free up cash, a sign of more acute financial strain amid persistently high prices and ongoing inflationary pressures.

    Sources indicate that the share of workers with an outstanding loan in the third quarter was 19.6%, up slightly from 19.5% in the previous quarter, according to Fidelity. The percentage of participants taking a new loan from their 401(k) held steady at 2.8%.

    Separately, the share of workers taking a hardship withdrawal rose to 2.17% from 2.12% in the second quarter, Fidelity found.

    In a recent development, "There is a rise because of economic reasons," noted Philip Chao, a certified financial planner and chief investment officer at Experiential Wealth, based in Cabin John, Maryland. "No question about it.".

    In a recent development, A hardship withdrawal can be taken from a retirement initiative without paying an early withdrawal penalty as long as the investor has an "immediate and heavy financial need," according to the IRS, such as avoiding foreclosure, eviction or unforeseen health expenses. Such distributions are also typically taxable.

    In a recent development, so-called leakage from 401(k) looks, particularly when workers cash out their accounts before retirement, can significantly erode long-term wealth by undermining the power of compound growth. Withdrawing funds during a market downturn can be especially damaging, making it more difficult to recover losses and benefit from a future rebound, financial advisors say.

    "This is not a piggy bank," Chao noted.

    However, despite the general consensus that savers shouldn't tap their retirement accounts, there may be situations in which investors don't have another good option, Chao said.

    In other words, the financial "ideal" doesn't align with "reality" for households, he remarked.

    Retirement plan withdrawals are happening as rising inflation has pressured households' wages and savings, other data also shows.

    "Real" average hourly earnings — or wages after accounting for the rising cost of living — fell 0.7% in the year through September 2026, according to the latest annual figures published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

    Households are saving at their lowest rate since 2022, and consumers are increasingly turning to debt such as credit cards to make ends meet.

    Fidelity said earlier this year that 401(k) investors took more loans in 2025 relative to 2024. The findings are consistent with other reports as well.

    Vanguard Group, another 401(k) administrator, noted in an annual report that savers took a record number of hardship withdrawals last year.

    A separate report issued this month by the Plan Sponsor Council of America, a trade group representing employers, found that the share of 401(k) participants with a loan outstanding from their workplace retirement plan rose "significantly" in 2025, nearly doubling from about 12% the prior year.

    The percentage of 401(k) investors who took a hardship withdrawal from their plan also increased for the third consecutive year, to 3.4% in 2025 from 1.5% in 2022, according to the PSCA report.

    Such "401(k) loans and hardships are there for participants when they need to tap the funds," stated Hattie Greenan, the PSCA's research director. "Clearly there's a need right now.".

    There are situations in which a retirement blueprint withdrawal could be OK for workers, Chao said.

    For example, 401(k) loans are generally a cheaper form of borrowing than credit cards, because investors ultimately pay themselves back with interest, he mentioned.

    According to recent reports, "If you just need it for a month, two, three, that's fine," Chao noted. "It's not going to kill you, borrowing from yourself.".

    However, a 401(k) loan may make sense only if the saver believes they'll be able to repay it, he stated.

    Failure to repay a loan can lead to income taxes and penalties that erode long-term savings, Chao remarked.

    Depending on the specific terms of a workplace retirement initiative, investors who are laid off or leave their job may have to repay their full loan relatively quickly. Just 34% of intends allow for continued repayment of a loan after separation from service, according to the PSCA report.

    #96940. Tech Report: Stuck: How a frozen housing market is hitting buyers, sellers and the economy

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1449 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Stuck: How a frozen housing market is hitting buyers, sellers and the economy

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1449 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that autumn is usually a busy time in the housing market, but not this year.
    • Buyers and sellers are moving to the sidelines, leaving those in the real estate business without much business.
    • The average rate on the popular 30-year fixed mortgage hovered around 6.60% in July, according to Mortgage News Daily.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that autumn is usually a busy time in the housing market, but not this year. A sharp spike in mortgage rates in September has pushed the already chilly real estate sector into a deep freeze.

    Buyers and sellers are moving to the sidelines, leaving those in the real estate business without much business.

    It seems like everyone is stuck.

    The average rate on the popular 30-year fixed mortgage hovered around 6.60% in July, according to Mortgage News Daily. By the start of October, it was at 7.61%, a full percentage point higher.

    "That shock, that rise of 100 basis points, is one of the fastest three-month increases we've seen in decades," mentioned Zillow CEO Jeremy Wacksman on CNBC.

    It has been revealed that while the jump in rates exacerbated the problem, the slowdown in the housing market has been building for years. Rising home prices have pushed the dream of homeownership out of reach for a growing number of Americans. The number of active buyers nationally has been declining for six straight months and in October hit its lowest level since the aftermath of the financial crisis, according to Redfin.

    The supply of homes for sale is also low. Builders are now faced with higher costs for land, labor, materials and energy. They simply can't afford to build the cheaper homes that are right now in demand. Single-family building permits, an indicator of future construction, were down 13% in October year over year, according to the U.S. Census. And builder sentiment in November dropped to the lowest level since 2012.

    This slowdown in the entire housing ecosystem is impacting every facet of Americans' lives and livelihoods.

    In a recent development, "Where you live determines so much. It determines where your kids go to school. It determines the jobs that you have access to, right? It determines whether or not you're able to be close to your family," mentioned Chen Zhao, chief economist at Redfin. "What we've seen with the housing market these past four years, with this historically low level of turnover, is that a lot of people really are stuck in their home.".

    Closed sales of existing homes fell to a 16-year low in October, according to the National Association of Realtors. Pending sales, an indicator of future closings, hit a record low on the 25-year-old index from the Realtors.

    While the pace of home price increases has slowed recently, prices are up well over 50% from pre-pandemic levels. Part of that is because homebuilding has slowed to a crawl.

    It all has Ryan Deighan, who wants to buy a home, wondering if he ever will.

    "I genuinely don't know, and that's the scary part," he said.

    It has been revealed that deighan and his wife have been renting in Boston for six years. He is a chiropractor; she works in private equity. Even with a combined salary of more than $200,000 a year, he says they're stuck.

    "Making what I am and what my wife makes, it just feels like we're on paper doing well, but it feels like we are still kind of fighting to put down certain amounts toward a house," Deighan mentioned.

    Being priced out of homeownership, he remarked, is changing what he called his "checklist" of how he once pictured his future.

    In a recent development, "You graduate college, you find someone, you get married, you have the home with the white picket fence and the dog, and then the kids," he mentioned. "That just looks a little different for us.".

    According to recent reports, the numbers don't just affect would-be buyers. They are hitting sellers, too.

    It has been revealed that robin Welch has been living in her Cleveland-area home for more than 20 years. Her children are now grown and moved out. She would like to downsize to a condominium, but the math doesn't make sense — in part, because her current interest rate is much lower than any new rate she could get. This has been dubbed the mortgage "lock-in effect.".

    Industry observers note that "It actually costs more money to buy less of a home," remarked Welch. "I would have to pay into an HOA, which would be another monthly expense on top of increased property taxes and increased interest rate.".

    Welch has also done upgrades to her home over the years and doesn't want to have to start doing that on another home.

    CNBC's Property Play with Diana Olick covers new and evolving opportunities for the real estate investor, delivered weekly to your inbox.

    Welch is part of why the housing turnover rate, which is how often homes get new owners, has now dropped to just 3.8% a year, well below the 5% rate in the decade following the financial crisis, according to Cotality.

    In addition, the national mobility rate, which is how often people move from region to region, has been falling for two years. It now sits at 8.3%, down from 11.1% a decade ago, according to Harvard's Joint Center for Housing Studies tabulations of U.S. Census Bureau data. Mobility hit a high of nearly 18% in the late 1980s.

    Industry observers note that "It's largely because of the interest lock-in effect, but also because of home prices just being so high," noted Riordan Frost, senior research analyst at Harvard's JCHS. "Those things combined have made it hard both for existing homeowners to move and for people to get into homeownership.".

    Recent findings suggest that americans have nearly $35 trillion of their wealth locked up in housing, a record high, according to Cotality. But the slowdown in the housing market, Frost remarked, impacts the accumulation, handover and use of that wealth. It also affects the labor market.

    "Any kind of potential job would have to really outweigh … the price of taking that mortgage with a higher rate, or the price of moving, or the price of getting into a higher rent unit," Frost said.

    The wealth gap between homeowners and renters now is nothing short of massive. The most recent survey of consumer finances last year by the Federal Reserve revealed that the median homeowner net wealth is about 43 times the median renter net wealth.

    Sources indicate that "It has kind of knock-on effects for the rest of the economy. It has effects on the labor market and how good of a match we can get between employees and employers. It has an effect on education. It has an effect on just GDP growth," mentioned Zhao.

    When homes aren't selling and people aren't moving, those who work in that business are stuck as well. The entire housing ecosystem is churning much more slowly, and the sudden jump in mortgage rates is causing deals to fall apart.

    Industry observers note that "Right after Labor Day, we went live with a bunch of listings. They all went under contract over the asking price," noted Dana Bull, a real estate agent in the Boston suburbs. But then rates spiked.

    "It was a shock to the system," Bull said. "I think all of them came back on the market. We fell out of contract." Asked if she is seeing colleagues leaving the market, she answered: "People are thinking about it. It's tough.".

    Recent findings suggest that the economy has lost close to 2,000 jobs in real estate and leasing over the past year and 4,400 jobs in residential construction, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

    It has been revealed that jobs in the mortgage industry have been falling since June and are down 38% since their last peak in the second quarter of 2021, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association. That was when mortgage rates were less than half what they are today.

    Shant Banosian, president of Rate and the top mortgage originator in the U.S. by dollar volume, said his business is down about 30% this past year.

    According to recent reports, "Whenever change happens quickly, there's a slowdown," stated Banosian, who has been in the business for 23 years. "It requires more of us to go out and advise, educate and guide. So, what I experienced was I just needed to spend more time on marketing, branding, relationship building. The conversations are longer because people want more information to try to navigate this market.".

    Sources indicate that bull agrees. She stated her job has gotten harder as well.

    "We've done double the work this year, having homes go under contract, fall out of contract, putting them back under agreement, but definitely more negotiating," she said. "That's sort of my plea to both buyers and sellers: We need to get back to a space where we're comfortable negotiating.".
